ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r1.claim: The Prophet reproaches Ubay for not answering when he called him while Ubay was praying, citing the revealed command to respond to God and the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r1.anchor: لأبي حين دعاه وهو في الصلاة متلبث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r2.claim: Mujahid and most commentators identify life-giving response with obeying the Qur'an's commands and prohibitions, yielding eternal life and bliss; the author prefers this in context as beneficial instruction that leads to good in both lives.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r2.anchor: المعنى استجيبوا للطاعة وما تضمنه القرآن من أوامر ونواهي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r3.claim: Alternative explanations of “what gives you life” are fighting unbelievers, which prevents defeat and death; martyrdom, according to Ibn Ishaq; religious knowledge; truth, also reported from Mujahid; worldly elevation; war spoils and livelihood; or bodily life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r3.anchor: لما يحييكم هو مجاهدة الكفار لأنهم لو تركوها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r4.claim: The initial lam may attach to the Messenger's call, since “call” takes lam; others make lam mean “to” and attach it to “respond,” distinguishing the two prepositions' functions. Poetry illustrates the syntax.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p301/r4.anchor: والظاهر تعلق لما بقوله دعاكم ودعا يتعدى باللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r1.claim: The author identifies ʿAli ibn ʿIsa as al-Rummani and describes his preceding interpretation as following a Muʿtazili approach.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r1.anchor: وعلي بن عيسى هو الرماني وهو معتزلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God may control a person's heart, turn cowardice to courage, or protect a believer from intended sins; he interprets the hadith of the heart between God's fingers as two effects of lordship. It may also mean God knows every thought.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r2.anchor: وتأويله بين أثرين من آثار ربوبيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r3.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that God owns hearts more completely than people do and can intervene between each person and heart by His will; the author's broader sense is God's control over all things and ability to thwart desire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r3.anchor: واختار الطبري أن يكون المعنى إن الله أخبر أنه أملك لقلوب العباد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r4.claim: One interpretation says God protects believers from sins that their hearts intend through divine preservation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r4.anchor: يحول بين المؤمن وبين المعاصي التي يهم بها قلبه بالعصمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r5.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r5.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq reads “between the person” with kasra on mīm, following the inflection; Hasan and al-Zuhri read “between the person” without hamza, with the hamza's vowel shifted and r geminated by extending pause pronunciation into connected speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r5.anchor: بين المرء بكسر الميم إتباعا لحركة الإعراب إذ في المرء لغتان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r6.claim: The pronoun in “and to Him you will be gathered” apparently refers to God, though it may be a pronoun of circumstance; resurrection brings reward and punishment and reminds hearers of their final outcome.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p303/r6.anchor: الظاهر أن الضمير في أنه عائد إلى الله ويحتمل أن يكون ضمير الشأن

SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.claim: In هذا الرجل منطلق, الرجل is an adjective/appositive to هذا; together they function like one noun, equivalent to هذا منطلق.
SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.anchor: فالرجل صفة لهذا وهما بمنزلة اسم ~~واحد كأنك قلت هذا منطلق

SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.claim: In هذا الرجل منطلقا, الرجل is built on the demonstrative and منطلقا is a circumstantial accusative describing a previously known man.
SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.anchor: وأما النصب فقولك هذا الرجل منطلقا جعلت الرجل مبنيا على هذا

SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.claim: In هو الحق مصدقا, الحق cannot modify the pronoun هو; مصدقا is therefore a circumstantial accusative, since a pronoun is not qualified by an overt noun.
SIBAWAYH:فأماالرفعفقولكهذاالرجلمنطلقفالر.anchor: لهو من قبل أن هو اسم مضمر والمضمر لا يوصف بالمظهر أبدا

SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r1.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r1.claim: The common reading has fatḥa on mīm; Ibn Abi Ishaq reads kasra by matching it to the hamza's vowel.
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r1.anchor: العامة على فتح الميم، وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق بكسرها على إتباعها لحركة الهمزة

SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r2.claim: The most eloquent dialect keeps mīm fatḥa in every case; the other follows case endings, with damma nominative, fatḥa accusative, and kasra genitive.
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r2.anchor: أن في " المرء " لغتين أفصحهما على فتح الميم مطلقا. والثانية بإتباع الميم لحركة الإعراب

SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r3.speaker: الحسن والزهري
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Zuhri read with fatḥa on mīm and a doubled rāʾ, explained by moving the hamza's vowel to rāʾ and treating connection as pause.
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والزهري بفتح الميم وتشديد الراء. وتوجيهها أن يكون نقل حركة الهمزة إلى الراء

SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r4.claim: In وأنه, the pronoun may be one of affair or refer to God; the latter is better because الله immediately precedes it.
SAMIN-DURR:8:24/r4.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الهاء ضمير الأمر والشأن، وأن تعود على الله تعالى، وهو الأحسن لقوله " الله "

ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r1.claim: What gives life can mean knowledge, which is a cause of life.
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r1.anchor: أي لما يكون سببا للحياة وهو العلم

ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r2.claim: Alternatively, it can mean what causes lasting life in the bliss of the afterlife.
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r2.anchor: وجائز أن يكون لما يكون سببا للحياة الدائمة، في نعيم الآخرة

ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r3.claim: Istajībū has the sense of ajībū, answer or respond.

ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r4.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r4.claim: The poet's phrase lam yastajibhu means that no one answered the caller, illustrating the synonymy of istajāba and ajāba.
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r4.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندا.

ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r5.claim: One view says God comes between a believer and disbelief, and between a disbeliever and faith by death, blocking what a person keeps putting off.
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم يحول بين المؤمن والكفر، ويحول بين الكافر والإيمان بالموت

ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r6.claim: A second view takes the phrase to mean that God is near each person at this degree, like the statement that He is nearer than the jugular vein.
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r6.anchor: أن الله مع المرء في القرب بهذه المنزلة

ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r7.claim: A further explanation is that God can replace believers' fear of the enemy with security, and make their apparently confident enemy weak and fearful.
ZAJJAJ:v2p409/r7.anchor: فأعلم الله جل ثناؤه أنه يحول بين المرء وقلبه بأن يبدله بالخوف الأمن

ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r1.speaker: Raghib
ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r1.claim: Raghib explains that God can intervene between a person's desires and their outward action, turning the person away from the heart's urge.
ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r1.anchor: God can turn man away from what his heart urges him to do (Raghib).

ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r2.claim: God-consciousness alone prevents wrongful desires from misleading a person and making them like those who do not reason.
ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r2.anchor: it is God-consciousness alone that can prevent man from being misled by wrong desires and, thus, from becoming like

ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r3.claim: The call to what gives life means spiritual awareness of right and wrong together with the will to act on it.
ASAD-NOTES:8:24#n24/r3.anchor: that is, spiritual awareness of right and wrong and the will to act accordingly.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r1.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r1.claim: Al-Jurjani says unqualified interpretation without knowledge brought confusion and harm; those who avoided such speculation would at least have done no damage.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r1.anchor: ولم يخوضوا فى التفسير ولم يتعاطوا التأويل، لكان البلاء واحداً ولكانوا إذا لم يبنوا لم يهدموا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r2.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r2.claim: Al-Jurjani portrays knowledge as a faithful friend that should not be abandoned when adversity makes learning difficult.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r2.anchor: فالعلم الذى هو صديق لا يحول عن العهد ولا يدغل فى الود، وصاحب لا يصح عليه النكث والغدر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r3.claim: Bint al-Shati says al-Jurjani believed he had decisively demonstrated the unsurpassed eloquence of Quranic composition in a concrete, graspable form and urged readers to study his book.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p24/r3.anchor: وظن الجرجاني أنه قطع قول كل دارس وجاء فى بيان فوت نظم القرآن بما قصر عنه الأوائل والأواخر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p27.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p27.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p27.claim: Verses 20–28 continue the gradual instruction, purification, and reform of believers, openly warning those whose weaknesses prompted the directives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p27.anchor: The ongoing subject of instructing, purifying and reforming the believers continues with its gradual revelations in the succeeding verses.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p27.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p27.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p27.claim: The whole Muslim community must stay alert: if some spread mischief and others fail to stop them, the harm will ultimately engulf everyone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p27.anchor: others did not try to stop them, then ultimately this mischief will embrace everyone

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p28.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p28.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p28.claim: Muḥammad invites people to true life, and they should follow his invitation wholeheartedly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p28.anchor: Muḥammad (sws) is inviting them to true life. They should whole-heartedly follow it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p28.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p28.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p28.claim: Those who refuse the Messenger after hearing and understanding his preaching face God's law intervening between them and their hearts, which are then sealed forever.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p28.anchor: Those who do not open their hearts to his preaching even after listening to it and understanding it will find the law of God become a barrier between them and their hearts.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.claim: The life offered by God's call is spiritual life: accepting truth grants insight and intellect, and revives the heart; refusal leaves disbelievers dead with respect to their purpose of creation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.anchor: real life is the life of his heart and his soul. If he loses the ability to contemplate the truth and refuses to accept it, he is actually dead with respect to his purpose of creation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.speaker: Jesus
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.claim: Jesus is quoted as teaching that human beings live not on bread alone but on every word from God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.anchor: Jesus is reported to have said: “Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.claim: God's being a barrier between a person and his heart means that God's law and practice become the barrier; effects caused by that law are attributed to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.anchor: God becoming a barrier here means God’s law become a barrier. At times, things that happen because of God’s law and practice are ascribed to God Himself.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.claim: A person can turn back from vice up to a limit, but beyond it the heart becomes uncontrollable; turning from a Messenger's powerful call brings the law that seals hearts into effect.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.anchor: When a person starts to indulge in vices, then until a certain limit he can still turn back if he pays heed; however, when this limit is crossed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.claim: Weak and hypocritical Muslims still have time to reform; otherwise their hearts will be sealed and tarnished beyond recovery, and they must consider their coming judgment before God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p31.anchor: they still have the time to mend their ways. Otherwise, their hearts will be sealed. They will be tarnished to such an extent that it they will never be able to regain their lustre.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p32.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p32.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p32.claim: The group that professes truth but cannot meet its demands is warned that failure to reform will let God's law become a barrier between them and their hearts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p32.anchor: if they do not mend their affairs, the law of God becomes a barrier between them and their hearts.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r1.speaker: معمر
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r1.claim: Maʿmar compares God’s intervening between a person and his heart with the statement that God is nearer than the jugular vein.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r1.anchor: عن معمر في قوله تعالى ﴿ يحول بين المرء وقلبه ﴾ قال هي كقوله ﴿ أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد ﴾

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r2.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says God intervenes between a believer and disbelief, and between an unbeliever and faith.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r2.anchor: معمر قال الكلبي يحول بين المؤمن وبين الكفر وبين الكافر والإيمان

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr likewise says God intervenes between a believer and disbelief, and between an unbeliever and faith.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله تعالى ﴿ يحول بين المرء وقلبه ﴾ قال بين المؤمن وبين الكفر وبين الكافر وبين الإيمان

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r4.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says God intervenes between an unbeliever and obedience to God, and between a believer and disobedience to God.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p257/r4.anchor: عن عبد العزيز بن أبي رواد عن الضحاك بن مزاحم قال سمعته قال يحول بين المرء وقلبه قال يحول بين الكافر وطاعة الله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r1.claim: Repeating the address and naming their faith stirs believers to obey the coming commands and reminds them of what in them calls for obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r1.anchor: تكرير النداء مع وصفهم بنعت الإيمان لتنشيطهم إلى الإقبال على الامتثال

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r2.claim: Respond to God and the Messenger through good obedience; the Messenger directly delivers God's call.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r2.anchor: بحسن الطاعة ( إذا دعاكم ( أي الرسول إذ هو المباشر لدعوة الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r3.claim: One explanation is that the call leads through beliefs and deeds to everlasting life in lasting bliss.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r3.anchor: أي لما يورثكم الحياة الأبدية في النعيم الدائم من العقائد والأعمال

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r4.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r4.claim: Another explanation is jihad, through which God gave believers honor after humiliation, strength after weakness, and protection after subjugation.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r4.anchor: كما روى ذلك عن عروة بن الزبير

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r5.claim: Calling beliefs, deeds, and jihad “life” is metaphor or metonymy, naming the cause for its effect.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r5.anchor: إما استعارة أو مجاز مرسل بإطلاق السبب على المسبب

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r6.speaker: القتبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r6.claim: Al-Qutaybī says the phrase means martyrdom, also figuratively.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r6.anchor: القتبي : المراد به الشهادة وهو مجاز أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r7.claim: Qatāda identifies what gives life as the Qurʾān.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r7.anchor: قتادة : القرآن وقال أبو مسلم : الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r8.claim: Abū Muslim identifies what gives life as Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r8.anchor: قتادة : القرآن وقال أبو مسلم : الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r9.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r9.claim: Several authorities take it as religious knowledge, the basis of everlasting life, while ignorance is true death; the metaphor is familiar in literature and rhetoric.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r9.anchor: غير واحد : هو العلوم الدينية التي هي مناط الحياة الأبدية كما أن الجهل مدار الموت الحقيقي

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's couplet likens the ignorant person to a dead person, illustrating ignorance as death.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r10.anchor: وللزمخشري : لا تعجبن لجهول حلته فذاك ميت وثوبه كفن

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r11.claim: The verse is cited as requiring a worshipper to answer the Prophet when he calls during prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r11.anchor: واستدل بالآية على وجوب إجابته صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إذا نادى أحدا وهو في الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r12.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r12.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that answering the Prophet does not invalidate prayer, since it too is a response.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r12.anchor: وعن الشافعي أن ذلك لا يبطلها لأنها أيضا إجابة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r13.speaker: الروياني
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r13.claim: Al-Rūyānī transmits the view that answering is not obligatory and does invalidate prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r13.anchor: وحكى الروياني أنها لا تجب وتبطل الصلاة بها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r14.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r14.claim: Another view permits breaking prayer when delay would cause urgent harm, such as failing to warn a blind person at a well.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r14.anchor: وقيل : إنه يقطع الصلاة إذا كان الدعاء لأمر يفوت بالتأخير كما إذا رأى أعمى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r15.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r15.claim: Al-Tirmidhī and al-Nasāʾī report from Abū Hurayra that the Prophet called Ubayy ibn Kaʿb during prayer; Ubayy hurried to him, the Prophet cited this verse, then promised to teach him al-Fātiḥa as the greatest sūra and seven oft-repeated verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r15.anchor: وأيد القول بالوجوب بما أخرجه الترمذي والنسائي عن أبي هريرة أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم مر على أبي بن كعب وهو يصلي فدعاه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r16.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the report does not establish that answering leaves prayer intact; the call may have concerned an urgent matter for which interruption was allowed.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r16.anchor: وأنت تعلم أنه لا دلالة فيه على أن إجابته صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r17.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r17.claim: Al-Rāghib explains ḥawl as change or separation, with the verb shifting in usage accordingly.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r17.anchor: كما قال الراغب تغير الشيء وانفصاله عن غيره وباعتبار التغير قيل حال الشيء يحول

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r18.claim: Literal separation is inapplicable to God, so the phrase figuratively conveys extreme nearness: the separator is nearer to both separated things than they are to one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r18.anchor: فهو مجاز عن غاية القرب من العبد لأن من فصل بين شيئين كان أقرب إلى كل منهما

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r19.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r19.claim: Many treat the expression as a representative metaphor; a dependent metaphor is also possible, with yaḥūlu meaning “draws near.”
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r19.anchor: كثير أن الكلام من باب الاستعارة التمثيلية ويجوز أن يكون هناك استعارة تبعية فمعنى يحول يقرب

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r20.claim: Al-Ālūsī also allows a compound metonymy for the implication of nearness, judging it the more fitting analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r20.anchor: بل ادعى أنه الأنسب وإرادة هذا المعنى هو المروي عن الحسن وقتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r21.claim: The nearness interpretation parallels the statement that God is nearer to a person than the jugular vein.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p190#2/r21.anchor: قوله سبحانه : ( ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r1.claim: The phrase also warns that God knows the heart's hidden contents, including matters its owner may overlook.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r1.anchor: وفيها تنبيه على أنه تعالى مطلع من مكنونات القلوب على ما قد يغفل عنه أصحابها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r2.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r2.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī reads it as a call to purify the heart promptly: death can intervene and remove the chance to treat its illnesses and restore it rightly.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r2.anchor: فمعنى يحول بينه وبين قلبه يميته فيفوته الفرصة التي هو واجدها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r3.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r3.claim: Many take it as a representative metaphor for God's control of hearts: He changes resolves and aims, inspires guidance or deviation, and turns security to fear and remembrance to forgetfulness.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r3.anchor: غير واحد : إنه استعارة تمثيلية لتمكنه تعالى من قلوب العباد فيصرفها كيف يشاء

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r4.speaker: أم سلمة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r4.claim: Through Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, Umm Salama asks about the Prophet's frequent prayer for firmness; he says every human heart is between God's fingers, and He establishes or makes it stray.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r4.anchor: كما في حديث شهر بن حوشب عن أم سلمة وقد سألت رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن إكثاره الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet explained the verse as God intervening between a believer and disbelief and between a disbeliever and guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : سألت النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن هذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r6.claim: The Prophetic answer likely names only the two greatest outcomes, happiness and misery; divine control extends beyond those examples.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r6.anchor: اقتصار على الأمرين اللذين هما أعظم مدار السعادة والشقاوة وإلا فهذا من فروع التمكن

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī polemically says God kept the ʿAdliyya from accepting this account and that they thereby left the straight path.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r7.anchor: وقد حال سبحانه بين العدلية وبين اعتقاد هذا فعدلوا عن سواء السبيل

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r8.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r8.claim: One scholar links the command to 8:23: those deaf to guidance cannot benefit from being made to hear, whereas believers were granted faith and obedience, so should answer and seize their chance before God intervenes between a person and faith or obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r8.anchor: وبين بعض الأفاضل ربط الآيات على ذلك بأنه تعالى لما نص بقوله عز من قائل : ( لو علم الله فيهم خيرا لأسمعهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes that this reconciliation carries a difficulty concerning moral responsibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r9.anchor: ولا يخفى ما فيه من التكليف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r10.claim: Another view places the command in the context of battle: despite fear and tight hearts, fight when called, knowing God can change fear and courage.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r10.anchor: وقيل : إن القوم لما دعوا إلى القتال والجهاد وكانوا في غاية الضعف والقلة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r11.claim: A reading doubles the rāʾ in al-marʾ by deleting the hamza and transferring its vowel, treating connected recitation like pause.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r11.anchor: بتشديد الراء على حذف الهمزة ونقل حركتها إليها وإجراء الوصل مجرى الوقف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r12.claim: The pronoun in wa-annahu may refer to God, or the clause may be impersonal: “and that you will be gathered to Him.”
ALUSI-FULL:v9p191/r12.anchor: أي الله عز وجل أو الشأن ( إليه تحشرون

ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r1.claim: You are gathered to God alone, who recompenses every rank of deed, none of which escapes His knowledge; therefore hasten to obey and respond.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r1.anchor: لا إلى غيره فيجازيكم بحسب مراتب أعمالكم التي لم يخف عليه شيء منها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r2.claim: One explanation emphasizes that gathering and recompense belong to God alone, so no effort should be spared in seizing the opportunity to obey.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r2.anchor: وقيل : المعنى أنه تحشرون إليه تعالى دون غيره فيجازيكم فلا تألوا جهدا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r3.claim: Another explanation joins God's control of hearts in this life to the impossibility of escape from Him in the next: submit and do not contemplate disobedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r3.anchor: أو المعنى أنه المتصرف في قلوبكم في الدنيا ولا مهرب لكم عنه في الآخرة فسلموا الأمر إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r4.claim: Some infer that God determines hearts and creates their motives, yet rewards and punishes the compelled; al-Ālūsī says the verse does not prove compulsion in its familiar sense, only that all affairs ultimately return to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p192/r4.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنه سبحانه لما أشار في صدر الآية إلى أن السعيد من أسعده والشقي من أضله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r1.claim: Respond to God and the Messenger by obeying them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r1.anchor: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r2.claim: The command means to respond to what gives you life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r2.anchor: {إذا دعاكم} الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، {لما يحييكم} أي: إلى ما يحييكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r3.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r3.claim: Al-Suddī identifies what gives life as faith, since the unbeliever is dead and faith gives him life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r3.anchor: قال السدي: هو الإيمان، لأن الكافر ميت فيحيا بالإيمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r4.claim: Qatāda identifies it as the Qurʾān, which gives life and brings salvation and protection in both abodes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو القرآن فيه الحياة وبه النجاة والعصمة في الدارين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r5.claim: Mujāhid identifies what gives life as the truth.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r6.claim: Ibn Isḥāq identifies it as fighting in God's cause, through which God gave the believers honor after humiliation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r6.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: هو الجهاد أعزكم الله به بعد الذل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r7.speaker: القتيبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r7.claim: Al-Qutaybī identifies it as martyrdom, citing the statement that martyrs are alive with their Lord and provided for.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r7.anchor: وقال القتيبي: بل الشهادة قال الله تعالى في الشهداء: "بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r8.claim: The Prophet called Ubayy ibn Kaʿb while he prayed; when Ubayy explained, the Prophet invoked this verse, and Ubayy promised to answer future calls even in prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344/r8.anchor: مر على أبي بن كعب، رضي الله عنه، وهو يصلي، فدعاه فعجل أبي في صلاته، ثم جاء فقال رسول الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿAṭāʾ say God intervenes between a believer and unbelief, and between an unbeliever and faith.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير وعطاء: يحول بين المؤمن والكفر، وبين الكافر والإيمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God intervenes between an unbeliever and obedience and between a believer and sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك: يحول بين الكافر والطاعة، ويحول بين المؤمن والمعصية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid says God may intervene so a person does not understand or know what he is doing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يحول بين المرء وقلبه فلا يعقل ولا يدري ما يعمل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r4.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says a person can believe or disbelieve only by God's permission.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: يحول بين الإنسان وقلبه فلا يستطيع أن يؤمن ولا أن يكفر إلا بإذنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r5.claim: Another explanation addresses a call to battle when the believers felt weak: God can replace fear with security and cowardice with courage.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو أن القوم لما دعوا إلى القتال في حالة الضعف ساءت ظنونهم واختلجت صدورهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r6.claim: All will be gathered to God, who will recompense them for their deeds.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r7.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet often prayed for God to keep his heart firm, explaining that hearts are between God's two fingers and He turns them as He wills.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p344#2/r7.anchor: يقول: "يا مقلب القلوب ثبت قلبي على دينك"

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r1.claim: Responding to God and the Messenger means obeying them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r2.claim: The pronoun is singular because the context just mentioned one caller, and God's call is heard through the Messenger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r2.anchor: وحد الضمير فيه لما سبق ولأن دعوة الله تسمع من الرسول

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet passed Abū while he was praying, called him, and Abū hurried in his prayer to answer; when asked why, he said he had been praying, and the Prophet cited what had been revealed to him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r3.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام مر على أبي وهو يصلي فدعاه فعجل في صلاته

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r4.claim: One explanation is that answering the Prophet does not interrupt prayer, since prayer itself is a response to God and the Messenger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r4.anchor: فقيل هذا لأن إجابته لا تقطع الصلاة فإن الصلاة أيضا إجابة

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r5.claim: Another explanation is that the call concerned an urgent matter; a worshipper may interrupt prayer for such a matter. The apparent hadith favors the first explanation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r5.anchor: وقيل لأن دعاءه كان لأمر لا يحتمل التأخير وللمصلي أن يقطع الصلاة لمثله

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r6.claim: What gives life may be religious knowledge, which revives the heart while ignorance is its death; a cited poem calls the ignorant person dead and his clothing a shroud.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r6.anchor: من العلوم الدينية فإنها حياة القلب والجهل موته

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r7.claim: The phrase can also mean beliefs and deeds that grant eternal life in lasting bliss, jihad that preserves the community from defeat and death, or martyrdom, as in 3:169.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r7.anchor: أو مما يورثكم الحياة الأبدية في النعيم الدائم من العقائد والأعمال، أو من الجهاد

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r8.claim: The wording pictures God's extreme nearness to a person, as in 50:16.

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r9.claim: It warns that God knows the heart's hidden contents, some of which its owner may overlook.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r9.anchor: وتنبيه على أنه مطلع على مكنونات القلوب مما عسى يغفل عنه صاحبها

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r10.claim: It may urge prompt sincerity and purification before God separates a person from the heart through death or another cause.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r10.anchor: أو حث على المبادرة إلى إخلاص القلوب وتصفيتها قبل أن يحول الله بينه وبين قلبه بالموت

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r11.claim: It may portray God's control over the heart: He can undo intentions and change aims, preventing unbelief for one destined for felicity or faith for one destined for misery.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r11.anchor: أو تصوير وتخييل لتملكه على العبد قلبه فيفسخ عزائمه ويغير مقاصده

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r12.claim: A reading doubles the rāʾ after deleting the hamza and transferring its vowel to rāʾ, applying connected speech like a pause in a dialect that uses this doubling.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r12.anchor: وقرىء " بين المرء " بالتشديد على حذف الهمزة وإلقاء حركتها على الراء

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:24/r13.claim: All will be gathered to God, who will recompense them for their deeds.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r8.claim: Because the disbelievers' punishment followed from refusing to respond, believers are told to answer so they do not share the disbelievers' fate at the gathering.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r8.anchor: ما مضى من نكال الكافرين مسببا عن عدم الاستجابة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r9.claim: The address identifies them as people who have professed faith with their tongues.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r10.claim: They must make their professed faith real by responding eagerly and wholeheartedly to God and His Messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r10.anchor: صدقوا دعواكم ذلك بإيجاد الإجابة إيجاد من هو في غاية الرغبة فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r11.claim: The Messenger was sent to all creation and only calls them to what God commands and to right guidance and good.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r11.anchor: وكان سبحانه لا يدعون إلا إلى صلاح ورشد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r12.claim: The lam instead of ilā signals how near the benefit of obedience is; the call gives moral life through faith and knowledge instead of the disbelievers' deafness, muteness, and lack of reason.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p200/r12.anchor: ولما كان اجتناء ثمرة الطاعة في غاية القرب

BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r1.claim: The command is not confined to initial belief or some religious duties; the cited reports apply the call to answer even while praying.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r1.anchor: فلم تجد فيما أوحي الله إلي أن

BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد ابن المعلى
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r2.claim: In a report in Bukhari's tafsir and elsewhere, Abu Saʿid ibn al-Muʿalla was praying and delayed answering the Prophet until he finished; the Prophet cited this verse, then taught him that al-Fatiha is the greatest sura, the seven oft-repeated and the mighty Qur'an given to him.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد ابن المعلى رضي الله عنه قال

BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Abu Hurayra that Ubayy ibn Kaʿb delayed answering the Prophet while praying; the Prophet cited the verse, and Ubayy promised not to repeat this. The report is graded hasan sahih.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r3.anchor: وللترمذي عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r4.claim: The same report says the Prophet offered to teach Ubayy a sura unmatched in Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur'an; Ubayy recited Umm al-Qur'an, and the Prophet identified it as the seven oft-repeated and the great Qur'an given to him.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه ( أن النبي

BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r5.claim: God can return each person to the state He knows in them: an apparent believer may become a defiant unbeliever, while an unbeliever may be led back to faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r5.anchor: فيرده إلى ما علم منه فيصير فيما كشفه الحال كافرا معاندا بعد أن كان في ظاهر الحال مؤمنا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r6.claim: The phrase's necessary closeness is a metonym for God's complete power to change people's intentions and desires.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r6.anchor: فكنى سبحانه بشدة القرب اللازم للحيلولة عن شدة الاقتدار على تبديل العزائم والمرادات

BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r7.claim: They should hasten to follow the Messenger while their hearts remain open to obedience, fearing that God may change their hearts.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r7.anchor: وهو تحريض على المبادرة إلى اتباع الرسول

BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r8.claim: The verse warns them about their final return to God after warning them about the outcome of their present state.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p201/r8.anchor: ولما خوفهم عاقبة الحال , حذرهم شأن المآل

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r1.claim: All are gathered only to God: responders join the believers, while those who turn away are counted among unbelievers even if they refuse only one ruling, because religion is indivisible.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r2.claim: The condition does not restrict the command to particular calls; it reminds believers to follow every call of the infallible Messenger, who has called them to every good.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r2.anchor: وقدم علم أن ) إذا ( ليست قيدا وإنما هي تنبيه على وجوب اتباعه في كل ما يدعو إليه لعصمته

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r3.claim: Al-Harali calls the general prophetic protection preservation under the prior revealed law; protection from faults in conveyance, degrading acts, and major sins is agreed, while minor sins are disputed and some allow a prohibited act as an unfinished preliminary.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r3.anchor: قال الحرالي في أواخر كتاب له في أصوال الفقه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r4.claim: The author says the Prophet Muhammad is elevated above the debate about whether prophets may commit minor sins.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r4.anchor: فإن المتحقق من أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما هو علو عن هذا المحل

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r5.claim: Al-Harali’s special protection for Muhammad makes his acts the source and indicator of rulings at each moment; they are not judged by prior law or his understanding of earlier practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r5.anchor: المعنى الثاني من العصمة رفع الحكم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بما حفظه الحافظ من ماضي ظاهر شرعته

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r6.claim: Abu Bakr and Ibn Umar exemplified close imitation, following even the Prophet’s way of turning his mount, yellow dye, and sandals.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r6.anchor: فمن كان يسبق إليه من أكبار الصحابة نحو من هذا المعنى

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r7.claim: When someone continued his prayer after being called, the Prophet corrected his assumption by citing this command to answer God and the Messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r7.anchor: أي بقوله : ألم تسمع الله يقول { استجيبوا لله وللرسول }

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r8.claim: The Prophet repeatedly ordered a man to descend and harvest; after the man cited daylight, he insisted a third or fourth time, illustrating the authority of his call.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r8.anchor: فقال له في الثالثة أو الرابعة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r9.claim: Since the Prophet’s act establishes its ruling, following him without first specifying the ruling is valid; an ambiguous intention to imitate may exceed acting on a ruling already clarified.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r9.anchor: فإذا وضح أن فعله مبدأ الحكم ومعلم الإنباء لزم صحة التأسي به على مطلق التأسي مع إبهام رتبة الحكم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r10.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r10.claim: While in Yemen, Ali set out for Mecca in the same state of consecration as the Prophet, an example of following his practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r10.anchor: أحرم علي رضي الله عنه وهو باليمن

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r11.claim: Apparently differing prophetic rulings reflect hearers’ incomplete grasp of his knowledge, not contradiction: valid jihad expiates sins before God, while a debt still requires satisfying its claimant.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r11.anchor: ثم ذكر له ما قال جبرائيل عليه السلام من استثناء الدين الدين مما أنزل على حكم أمر الله في محكم شرعته وسنته

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r12.claim: People who followed the Prophet’s initial directive about pollination obtained fruit for three years, then returned without pollination to an even better yield; the example illustrates acting on his instruction.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r12.anchor: فقد عمل بأول فتياه غير واحد ممن لم يتسرب في نفاد حكمه وصحته

BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r13.claim: A prophetic act that conveys an obligation saves from punishment; one that teaches nearness to God leads to His love. If its status is unclear, imitate while learning the intent.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p202/r13.anchor: فكل فعل فعله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فإن كان بياتا لواجب

BIQAI-FULL:v3p203/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p203/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p203/r1.claim: The command to follow the Messenger is linked to the promise that following him brings God’s love, as stated in 3:31; where an act’s status is unclear, imitate him and learn its intent.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p203/r1.anchor: وإن لم يتضح له مجمل منهما تأسى بها على إبهام بغنيه علمه وتعلموا به نيته

BIQAI-FULL:v3p203/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p203/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p203/r2.claim: An act specific to the Prophet must be explicitly identified as exclusive by God or the Prophet, as in the exception stated in 33:50.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p203/r2.anchor: وما كان مختصا به فلا بد من إظهار أمر اختصاصه بخطاب من الله سبحانه أو منه عليه السلام

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r1.claim: Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla reports that while he prayed in the mosque the Prophet called him, then cited this verse and asked why he had not answered.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد بن المعلى ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان في المسجد وانا اصلي ، فدعاني

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r2.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r2.claim: Urwa ibn al-Zubayr interprets what gives life as the battle through which God gave the community honor and strength and protected them from their enemies.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r2.anchor: عن عروة بن الزبير يا ايها الذين امنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول اذا دعاكم لما يحييكم اي الحرب

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses what gives life as the truth.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : لما يحييكم للحق

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r4.claim: Qatada identifies it as the Qur'an, which brings life, confidence, deliverance, and protection in this world and the next.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : اذا دعاكم لما يحييكم قال : هو هذا القران ، فيه الحياة والثقة والنجاة والعصمة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r5.claim: Al-Suddi identifies it as Islam, which revived people from the death of disbelief.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r5.anchor: عن السدى اما يحييكم ففي الاسلام ، احياهم بعد موتهم بعد كفرهم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq also interprets it as the battle that gave the believers honor and strength and protected them from being overcome by their enemies.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r6.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق اذا دعاكم لما يحييكم يقول : للحر ب الذي اعزكم الله بها بعد الذل

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r7.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says God's knowledge comes between a person and his heart.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1679/r7.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس قوله : واعلموا ان الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه قال : علمه يحول بين المرء وقلبه

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r1.claim: God intervenes between a believer and disbelief or disobedience, and between a disbeliever and faith or obedience.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس يحل بين المرء وقلبه قال : يحول بين المؤمن وبين الكفر ومعاصي الله

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r2.claim: God keeps believers from ruinous sin that merits destruction, while disbelievers miss obedience that would bring the good granted to God's allies; this is within prior knowledge and decree.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r2.anchor: سالت ابن عباس عن قول الله : يحول بين المرء وقلبه

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r3.claim: God comes between a person and his heart until He leaves the person unable to reason.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله : يحول بين المرء وقلبه حتى يتركه لا يعقل

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، عكرمة، أبو صالح، مجاهد، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r4.claim: They say God intervenes between a believer and disbelief and between a disbeliever and belief.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r4.anchor: وروى عن سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة وابي صالح ومجاهد والسدي انهم قالوا : يحول بين المؤمن ان يكفر وبين الكافر ان يؤمن

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r5.speaker: الضحاك، عطية، مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r5.claim: They say God intervenes between a disbeliever and obedience, and between a believer and sin.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك وعطية ومقاتل بن حيان : بين الكافر وبين طاعته ، وبين المؤمن ومعصيته

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r6.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r6.claim: God's knowledge is what intervenes between a person and his heart.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r6.anchor: عن الربيع في قوله : واعلموا ان الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه قال : علمه يحول بين المرء وقلبه

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r7.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r7.claim: Being gathered to God means that people return to Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1680/r7.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان وانه اليه تحشرون يعني : اليه ترجعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p310/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p310/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p310/r4.claim: The summons restates 8:20 after the sura's case for obedience: Badr showed its blessings, and the commands to stand firm, obey, and heed the Messenger lead to this concluding appeal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p310/r4.anchor: إعادة لمضمون قوله : { يأيها الذين ءامنوا أطيعوا الله ورسوله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p310/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p310/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p310/r5.claim: The Messenger's call gives life to the community, and responding to him gives hearts sacred powers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p310/r5.anchor: فإن في دعوته إياهم إحياء لنفوسهم وأعلمهم أن الله يكسب قلوبهم بتلك الاستجابة قوى قدسية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r1.claim: Life literally enables bodily perception and voluntary movement; metaphorically it is a quality that completes a thing's purpose, as plant growth animates land and knowledge and sound judgment animate intellect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r1.anchor: والحياة قوة بها يكون الإدراك والتحرك بالاختيار ويستعار الإحياء تبعا لاستعارة الحياة للصفة أو القوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r2.claim: Life and giving life can also mean preserving life by warding off its threats, as in the life-giving value of retribution and saving one person, cited at 2:179 and 5:32.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r2.anchor: وتستعار الحياة والإحياء لبقاء الحياة واستبقائها بدفع العوادي عنها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r3.claim: Here life is what perfects human beings: sound belief, noble character, guidance to good action, reform of individuals and society, courage, independence, freedom, and stable livelihood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r3.anchor: وهو إعطاء الإنسان ما به كمال الإنسان ، فيعم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r4.claim: Believers must answer the Messenger whether he asks them to come or calls for an action; 'for what gives you life' explains the benefit rather than limiting the call, since his summons always brings some human good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r4.anchor: فالآية تقتضي الأمر بالامتثال لما يدعو إليه الرسول سواء دعا حقيقة بطلب القدوم ، أم طلب عملا من الأعمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r5.claim: A report cited from the Sahih collections says Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla was praying in the mosque, did not answer the Prophet's call, then heard the verse cited before being taught the greatest surah, al-Fatiha.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد بنن المعلى ، قال : كنت أصلي في المسجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r6.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Abu Hurayra that the Prophet called Ubayy ibn Ka'b during prayer; Ubayy finished, and the Prophet cited the verse when asking why he had not answered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r6.anchor: وفي ( جامع الترمذي ) عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج على أبي بن كعب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r7.claim: The Prophet cites the command through إذا دعاكم, which supports Ibn Ashur's reading of لما يحييكم as an explanatory qualifier, not a restriction on which calls must be answered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r7.anchor: فوقفه على قوله : { إذا دعاكم } يدل على أن { لما يحييكم } قيد كاشف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the Ubayy report is also transmitted by Malik ibn Anas; Ibn Ashur clarifies that this is the same report found in al-Tirmidhi.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية : وهو مروي أيضا من طريق مالك بن أنس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports a similar incident with Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman during the Battle of the Trench; Ibn Ashur says multiple similar cases underline the special status of the Messenger's call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p312/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطية وروي أنه وقع نحوه مع حذيفة بن اليمان في غزوة الخندق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r1.claim: The Qur’an is a comprehensive, protected law, a lasting miracle, and a guardian and confirmer of earlier revelation; its signs reveal its truth over time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r1.anchor: فأنزل القرآن قانونا عاما معصوما ، وأعجز بعجائبه فظهرت يوما فيوما ، وجعله مصدقا لما بين يديه ومهيمنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r2.claim: Its guidance admonishes wrongdoers and promises the virtuous, while its preservation prevents alteration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r2.anchor: وما فرط فيه من شئ يعظ مسيئا ويعد محسنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r3.claim: Companions clarified the Qur’an and later scholars disclosed its secrets for the community.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r3.anchor: ثم قيض لتبيينه أصحابه الأشداء الرحماء ، وأبان أسراره من بعدهم في الأمة من العلماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r4.claim: The author undertook this tafsir to explain insights, general principles of law, and detailed moral excellences glimpsed through reflection and earlier commentary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r4.anchor: طمعا في بيان نكت من العلم وكليات من التشريع ، وتفاصيل من مكارم الأخلاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r5.claim: He long hesitated from fear of the work’s burdens and his own errors, then resolved to proceed after judicial and legal-advisory appointments renewed the opportunity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r5.anchor: وفيما أنا بين إقدام وإحجام ، أتخيل هذا الحقل مرة القتاد وأخرى الثمام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r6.claim: He aims to offer insights absent from earlier commentaries and judge between exegetical schools, since repetition would stop the Qur’an’s inexhaustible benefits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r6.anchor: فجعلت حقا علي أن أبدي في تفسير القرآن نكتا لم أر من سبقني إليها ، وأن أقف موقف الحكم بين طوائف المفسرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r7.claim: He favors refining and adding to earlier work, preserving predecessors’ achievements, rather than merely clinging to them or demolishing them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p5/r7.anchor: وهي أن نعمد إلى ما أشاده الأقدمون فنهذبه ونزيده ، وحاشا أن ننقضه أو نبيده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r9.claim: The address is to believing affirmers, without disagreement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r9.anchor: هذا الخطاب للمؤمنين المصدقين بلا خلاف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r10.claim: Istajābū means ajībū; conventionally istajāba takes a lām while ajāba does not, though istajāba can also occur without lām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r10.anchor: واستجيبوا بمعنى أجيبوا، ولكن عرف الكلام أن يتعدى استجاب بلام ويتعدى أجاب دوم لام،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r11.claim: The unidentified poet's line uses istajāb from a caller without a lām, attesting the less usual construction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r11.anchor: والشاهد قول الشاعر: [الطويل] وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندا ...

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r12.speaker: مجاهد والجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r12.claim: Mujahid and most commentators take this as obedience and the Qurʾan's commands and prohibitions; life is metaphorical, emerging from disbelief and ignorance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r12.anchor: قال مجاهد والجمهور: المعنى للطاعة وما تضمنه القرآن من أوامر ونواه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r13.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r13.claim: Another view says Islam, which Ibn ʿAtiyya considers weak because already-believing addressees are not told to enter Islam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r13.anchor: وقيل الإسلام وهذا نحو الأول ويضعف من جهة أن من آمن لا يقال له ادخل في الإسلام،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r14.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r14.claim: Another view says warfare and jihad, which bring honor, victory, and triumph and are therefore called life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r14.anchor: وقيل لما يحييكم معناه للحرب وجهاد العدو وهو يحيي بالعزة والغلبة والظفر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r15.claim: Islam, obedience, and similar acts also lead to everlasting life in the hereafter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r15.anchor: ويحيي أيضا كما يحيي الإسلام والطاعة وغير ذلك بأنه يؤدي إلى الحياة الدائمة في الآخرة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r16.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r16.claim: Al-Naqqash says the summons is to martyrdom.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p513#3/r16.anchor: وقال النقاش: المراد إذا دعاكم للشهادة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r1.claim: The verse connects life in this world with life in the hereafter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: فهذه صلة حياة الدنيا بحياة الآخرة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r2.claim: One reading is that God intervenes by death, so believers should hasten obedience and prepare for the resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r2.anchor:
ومنها أنه لما أمرهم بالاستجابة في الطاعة حضهم على المبادرة والاستعجال فقال:
واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه بالموت والقبض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r3.claim: The gathering to God urges believers to hasten obedience and provision for the Day of Resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r3.anchor: أي فبادروا الطاعات وتزودوها ليوم الحشر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r4.claim: Another reading is that God's power, encompassing knowledge, and control intervene between a person and the heart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r4.anchor: ومنها أن يقصد بقوله واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه إعلامهم أن قدرة الله وإحاطته وعلمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r5.claim: This reading urges watchfulness and fear before God, who knows hidden thoughts, paralleling Q 50:16; Qatada is cited for this interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r5.anchor: ويشبه على هذا التأويل هذا المعنى قوله تعالى: ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r6.claim: A further reading warns that failure to obey could bring the same separation between unbelievers and their hearts described in Q 8:23.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r6.anchor: ولا تأمنوا إن تفعلوا أن ينزل بكم ما نزل بالكفار من الحول بينهم وبين قلوبهم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r7.claim: The phrase may reassure believers that God can replace fear of the enemy with courage and strength and do the reverse for unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r7.anchor: ومنها أن يكون المعنى ترجية لهم بأن الله يبدل الخوف الذي في قلوبهم من كثرة العدو فيجعله جرأة وقوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r8.claim: This accords with God turning hearts, as reflected in the Prophet's oath.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r8.anchor: فإن الله هو مقلب القلوب كما كان قسم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r9.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r9.claim: Some explain la ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-llāh as no power to avoid disobedience or strength for obedience except through God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r9.anchor: قال بعض الناس ومنه لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله أي لا حول على معصية ولا قوة على طاعة إلا بالله،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r10.speaker: المفسرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r10.claim: Al-Tabari reports views such as God separating believers from unbelief and unbelievers from faith; Ibn ʿAtiyya says these do not fit the verse's wording.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r10.anchor: وقال المفسرون في ذلك أقوالا هي أجنبية من ألفاظ الآية حكاها الطبري،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r11.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r11.claim: Ibn Abi Ishaq reads al-marʾ with kasra on the mīm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p514/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق «بين المرء» بكسر الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r1.speaker: الحسن والزبيدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Zubaydi read bayna al-marr with an open mīm and doubled rāʾ bearing kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r1.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: وقرأ الحسن والزبيدي «بين المر» بفتح الميم وشد الراء المكسورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r2.claim: Tuḥsharūn means people are resurrected on the Day of Judgment.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r3.claim: A report transmitted by Malik ibn Anas and al-Nasaʾi says the Prophet called Ubayy ibn Kaʿb during prayer; Ubayy finished quickly, heard the verse cited, and promised always to answer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r3.anchor: وروي عن طريق مالك بن أنس والنسائي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دعا أبي بن كعب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r4.speaker: البخاري ومسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r4.claim: Al-Bukhari and Muslim identify the person praying in the incident as Abu Saʿid ibn al-Muʿalla rather than Ubayy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r4.anchor: وفي البخاري ومسلم أن ذلك وقع مع أبي سعيد بن المعلى،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r5.claim: A similar incident is also reported with Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman during the Battle of the Trench.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p515/r5.anchor: وروي أنه وقع نحوه مع حذيفة بن اليمان في غزوة الخندق.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r2.claim: The one calling them is the Messenger.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ إذا دعاكم ﴾ يعني الرسول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r3.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that it means everything to which the Messenger calls; a report from Abū Saʿīd ibn al-Muʿallā recounts the Prophet calling him from prayer and citing this verse, after which he came and promised not to repeat the delay.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r3.anchor: كل ما يدعو الرسول إليه وهو معنى قول أبي صالح عن ابن عباس وفي أفراد البخاري من حديث أبي سعيد بن المعلى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r4.claim: Mujāhid has two transmitted explanations: the truth, and faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r4.anchor: أنه الحق رواه شبل عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد والثالث أنه الإيمان رواه ورقاء عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r5.claim: Al-Suddī also identifies what gives life as faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r5.anchor: والثالث أنه الإيمان رواه ورقاء عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد وبه قال السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r6.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r6.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Zayd say it means following the Qurʾān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r6.anchor: أنه اتباع القرآن قاله قتادة وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r7.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r7.claim: Ibn Isḥāq identifies it as jihad.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba says jihad gives life by reviving their religion and exalting them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r8.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة هو الجهاد الذي يحيي دينهم ويعليهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r9.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ gives the broad gloss that it is the revival of their affairs, then offers five ways to understand that revival.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r9.anchor: والسادس أنه إحياء أمورهم قاله الفراء فيخرج في إحيائهم خمسة أقوال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r10.claim: One explanation of reviving their affairs is setting their worldly and otherworldly affairs right.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r10.anchor: أحدها أنه إصلاح أمورهم في الدنيا والآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r11.claim: Another explanation combines a good name in this world with everlasting life in the Hereafter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r11.anchor: والثاني بقاء الذكر الجميل لهم في الدنيا وحياة الأبد في الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r12.claim: A third explanation is the lasting continuation of their bliss in the Hereafter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r12.anchor: والثالث أنه دوام نعيمهم في الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r13.claim: A fourth explanation is that they become believers, since an unbeliever is like a dead person.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r13.anchor: والرابع أنه كونهم مؤمنين لأن الكافر كالميت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r14.claim: A fifth explanation is that jihad revives them after death because martyrs are alive, and it gives them honor after humiliation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p338/r14.anchor: والخامس أنه يحييهم بعد موتهم وهو على قول من قال هو الجهاد لأن الشهداء أحياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say God can separate a believer from unbelief and an unbeliever from faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r1.anchor: يحول بين المؤمن وبين الكفر وبين الكافر وبين الإيمان رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس وبه قال سعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through al-ʿAwfī, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Farrāʾ say God can separate a believer from disobedience and an unbeliever from obedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r2.anchor: يحول بين المؤمن وبين معصيته وبين الكافر وبين طاعته رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r3.claim: Mujāhid says God comes between a person and his heart so that he cannot reason; Ibn al-Anbārī urges prompt action because reason may disappear before one can secure the fruits of deeds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r3.anchor: يحول بين المرء وقلبه حتى لا يتركه يعقل قاله مجاهد قال ابن الانباري المعنى يحول بين المرء وعقله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r4.claim: Qatāda understands the clause to mean God is near to a person and knows every secret, as in 50:16.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r4.anchor: والرابع أن المعنى هو قريب من المرء لا يخفى عليه شيء من سره كقوله ﴿ ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد ﴾ وهذا معنى قول قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says no one can believe or disbelieve except by God’s permission.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r5.anchor: يحول بين المرء وقلبه فلا يستطيع إيمانا ولا كفرا إلا بإذنه قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba says God comes between a person and his desire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r6.anchor: يحول بين المرء وبين هواه ذكره ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r7.claim: Another explanation is that God blocks what a person hopes for in his heart, such as a long life or victory.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r7.anchor: يحول بين المرء وبين ما يتمنى بقلبه من طول العمر والنصر وغيره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r8.claim: Another explanation is that God comes between a person and his heart through death, so people should hasten to do good before it occurs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r8.anchor: يحول بين المر وقلبه بالموت فبادروا الأعمال قبل وقوعه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains that God intervenes through His knowledge of a person’s inward deeds; no thought can be hidden from Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r9.anchor: يحول بين المرء وقلبه بعمله فلا يضمر العبد شيئا في نفسه إلا والله عالم به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r10.claim: A further explanation is that God changes what He places in hearts, turning fear into security or security into fear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r10.anchor: يحول بين ما يوقعه في قلبه من خوف أو أمن فيأمن بعد خوفه ويخاف بعد أمنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r11.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r11.claim: Al-Zajjāj connects the verse to the Muslims’ fear at their small numbers against a large enemy: God can replace fear with security and enemy strength with weakness, showing that He turns hearts.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p339/r11.anchor: وحكى الزجاج أنهم لما فكروا في كثرة عدوهم وقلة عددهم فدخل الخوف قلوبهم أعلمه الله تعالى أنه يحول بين المرء وقلبه بأن يبدله بالخوف الأمن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p340/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p340/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p340/r1.claim: You will be gathered to God for recompense for your deeds.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r1.speaker: البخاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r1.claim: Al-Bukhari glosses istajibū as answer or obey.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r1.anchor: قال البخاري: {استجيبوا} أجيبوا، {لما يحييكم} لما يصلحكم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r2.speaker: البخاري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r2.claim: Al-Bukhari explains what gives life as that which sets people right.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r2.anchor: قال البخاري: {استجيبوا} أجيبوا، {لما يحييكم} لما يصلحكم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r3.claim: Abu Saʿid ibn al-Muʿalla was praying when the Prophet called him; after he finished, the Prophet cited this verse, then identified al-Fatiha as the greatest surah and the seven oft-repeated verses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد بن المعلى قال: كنت أصلي، فمر بي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فدعاني فلم آته حتى صليت، ثم أتيته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies what gives life as the truth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد في قوله: {لما يحييكم} قال: الحق.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r5.claim: Qatada identifies what gives life as the Quran, which contains salvation, protection, and life.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة {لما يحييكم} قال: هو هذا القرآن، فيه النجاة والتقاة (1) والحياة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says Islam gives people life after the death of unbelief.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r6.anchor: وقال السدي: {لما يحييكم} ففي الإسلام إحياؤهم بعد موتهم بالكفر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r7.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r7.claim: Urwa ibn al-Zubayr interprets the call as a call to battle, by which God honored the believers after humiliation, strengthened them after weakness, and protected them from their enemy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p34/r7.anchor: عن عروة بن الزبير: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم} أي: للحرب التي أعزكم الله تعالى بها بعد الذل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God intervenes between a believer and disbelief, and between a disbeliever and faith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يحول بين المؤمن وبين الكفر، وبين الكافر وبين الإيمان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r2.claim: Al-Hakim graded Ibn Abbas’s stopped report sound and said the two compilers did not include it; Ibn Mardawayh’s raised version is weak, so the stopped version is sounder.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r2.anchor: رواه الحاكم في مستدركه موقوفا، وقال: صحيح ولم يخرجاه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r3.speaker: مجاهد، وسعيد، وعكرمة، والضحاك، وأبو صالح، وعطية، ومقاتل بن حيان، والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r3.claim: Mujahid, Sa'id, Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, Atiyyah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and al-Suddi give Ibn Abbas’s explanation as well.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r3.anchor: وكذا قال مجاهد، وسعيد، وعكرمة، والضحاك، وأبو صالح، وعطية، ومقاتل بن حيان، والسدي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r4.claim: In another report, Mujahid says God may intervene between a person and their heart until the person can no longer reason.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r4.anchor: وفي رواية عن مجاهد في قوله: {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} حتى تركه لا يعقل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
