IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says a person can neither believe nor disbelieve unless God permits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: يحول بين الإنسان وقلبه، فلا يستطيع أن يؤمن ولا يكفر إلا بإذنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r6.claim: Qatadah compares this statement with God being nearer to a person than the jugular vein.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة هو كقوله: {ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir says Prophetic reports accord with this verse’s warning about hearts being turned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r7.anchor: وقد وردت الأحاديث عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بما يناسب هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r8.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet often prayed for the Turner of hearts to keep his heart firm in religion; he said hearts are between God’s fingers and He turns them as He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r8.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، رضي الله عنه، قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر أن يقول: " يا مقلب القلوب، ثبت قلبي على دينك"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r9.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the Anas report hasan; some transmitters give a route through Jabir, but Ibn Kathir judges the Anas route more sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r9.anchor: وحديث أبي سفيان عن أنس أصح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r10.speaker: بلال
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r10.claim: Bilal reports that the Prophet prayed for the Turner of hearts to keep his heart firm in religion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r10.anchor: عن بلال، رضي الله عنه، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يدعو: "يا مقلب القلوب ثبت قلبي على دينك"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir calls Bilal’s report good in its chain, though interrupted; he says it meets the Sunan compilers’ standard, although they did not include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p35/r11.anchor: هذا حديث جيد الإسناد إلا أن فيه انقطاعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r1.speaker: النواس بن سمعان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r1.claim: Al-Nawwas reports that every heart is between the fingers of the Merciful, who establishes or deviates it as He wills; the Prophet prayed for firm hearts and said the Scale is in the Merciful’s hand, lowered or raised.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r1.anchor: النواس بن سمعان الكلابي، رضي الله عنه، يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " ما من قلب إلا وهو

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r2.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet’s frequent prayer for a firm heart; he explained that God may lead a human heart astray or establish it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r2.anchor: أن عائشة قالت: دعوات كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعو بها: "يا مقلب القلوب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r3.speaker: أم سلمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r3.claim: Umm Salamah reports the Prophet’s prayer for firm hearts, his explanation that every human heart is between God’s fingers, and his teaching her a personal prayer for forgiveness, relief from anger, and protection from trials.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r3.anchor: سمعت أم سلمة تحدث: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يكثر في دعائه يقول: "اللهم يا مقلب القلوب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r4.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr reports that the hearts of Adam’s children are like one heart between the Merciful’s fingers, turned as He wills; the Prophet prayed for them to be turned to obedience.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p36/r4.anchor: عبد الله بن عمرو؛ أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " إن قلوب بني آدم بين إصبعين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p37/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p37/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p37/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that Muslim alone, alongside al-Nasa'i, included Abdullah ibn Amr’s report through Haywah ibn Shurayh; al-Bukhari did not include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p37/r1.anchor: انفرد بإخراجه مسلم عن البخاري، فرواه مع النسائي من حديث حيوة بن شريح المصري

JISHUMI:v4p2891/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r1.speaker: الحسن والزهري
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r1.claim: The common reading has a light hamzated rāʾ and fatḥa on mīm; al-Hasan doubles rāʾ without hamza, while al-Zuhri has ḍamma on mīm with hamza; all are dialect forms.
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: بين المرء وقلبه بفتح الميم

JISHUMI:v4p2891/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r2.claim: استجابة and إجابة are synonymous; another view makes istijāba seeking an answer, though the cited line uses it to mean answering.
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r2.anchor: الاستجابة والإجابة بمعنى، وقيل: الاستجابة: طلب الإجابة

JISHUMI:v4p2891/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses فلم يستجبه to mean that no one answered the caller.
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر: وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندى

JISHUMI:v4p2891/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r13.claim: God commands compliance with His call and warns against disobeying His command.
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r13.anchor: ثم أمر - تعالى - بإجابة دعائه وحذر

JISHUMI:v4p2891/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r14.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Zajjaj gloss استجيبوا as أجيبوا; answering God means obeying His commands and prohibitions.
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r14.anchor: قيل: أجيبوا، عن أبي عبيدة والزجاج. وإجابته طاعته

JISHUMI:v4p2891/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r15.claim: Another gloss is to persist in obedience whenever God and the Messenger call; the lām means إلى.
JISHUMI:v4p2891/r15.anchor: داوموا على ما أنتم عليه من الإجابة لله وللرسول

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r1.speaker: السدي
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says faith gives life after their death in disbelief, so the call is to faith and obedience, the life of the soul.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r1.anchor: الإيمان يحييهم بعد موتهم أي كفرهم، عن السدي

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r2.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r2.claim: Mujahid explains what gives life as the truth.

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r3.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r3.claim: Mujahid also identifies it as Quran, which brings life, salvation, and protection in this world and the next.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r3.anchor: هو القرآن في الحياة والنجاة والعصمة في الدنيا والآخرة، عن مجاهد

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق والفراء وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq, al-Farra, and Abu Ali say it is jihad, which revives their cause and exalts their religion through God's support against the enemy.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r4.anchor: هو الجهاد؛ أي: دعاكم إلى إحياء أمركم وإعزاز دينكم

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r5.claim: Another interpretation is knowledge and action, through which people find guidance and attain ranks.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو العلم والعمل، أي: يحييكم بالعلم والعمل

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r6.speaker: القتبي
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r6.claim: Al-Qutbi says it means martyrdom and cites the promise that martyrs are alive with their Lord and provided for.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r6.anchor: الشهادة، عن [القتبي]، وقرأ: (بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون)

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r7.claim: Abu Muslim says it is the Garden and the lasting life and eternal bliss it entails.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r7.anchor: إلى الجنة وما يورثكم فيها من الحياة الدائمة ونعيم الأبد، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r8.speaker: أبو علي وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r8.claim: Abu Ali and Abu Muslim say God prevents benefit from the heart through death, loss of reason, or another affliction, so missed opportunities cannot be recovered; this urges prompt obedience.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r8.anchor: يفرق بين المرء والانتفاع بقلبه بالموت أو إذهاب اللب

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r9.claim: Another view is that God stands between a person and what the heart wishes: lifespan blocks hope and decree blocks planning.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r9.anchor: يحول بين المرء وبين ما يتمناه ويريد بقلبه

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r10.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r10.claim: Qatada takes it to mean God is nearer than the jugular vein and nothing is hidden from Him; this is a grave warning.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r10.anchor: أراد أنه أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد لا يخفى عليه

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r11.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r11.claim: Al-Asamm says God turns hearts between states: the Companions feared death in jihad, so God would replace fear with security by intervening between them and that fear.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r11.anchor: وأعلمهم الله أنه يبدل خوفهم أمنا بأن يحول بينهم

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r12.claim: It cannot mean that God prevents belief: He calls people to faith, promises reward and threatens for rejecting it, so the servant must be the responder rather than God answering His own call.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r12.anchor: ولا يجوز حمله على المنع من الإيمان؛ لأن الظاهر بخلافه

JISHUMI:v4p2893/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r13.claim: All are gathered for recompense, good for good and evil for evil; therefore one must hasten to obedience and repentance.
JISHUMI:v4p2893/r13.anchor: تجمعون إلى الجزاء إن خيرا فخير، وإن شرا فشر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.claim: The pronoun is singular because responding to the Messenger is responding to God; mentioning both reinforces the point.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.anchor: وحد الضمير كما وحده فيما قبله ، لأن استجابة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كاستجابته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.claim: Responding means obeying and complying; the call is a summons and exhortation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بالاستجابة . الطاعة والامتثال . وبالدعوة : البعث والتحريض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet called Ubayy ibn Kaʿb while he prayed; Ubayy hurried his prayer and promised always to answer such a call.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة : ( 419 ) أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r4.claim: One legal view makes answering the Prophet’s call a privilege specific to him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r4.anchor: وفيه قولان ، أحدهما : إن هذا مما اختص به رسول الله صلى الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r5.claim: Another view says the Prophet’s call concerned an urgent matter; a person praying may interrupt prayer if a comparable urgent call occurs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r5.anchor: والثاني أن دعاءه كان لأمر لم يحتمل التأخير ، وإذا وقع مثله للمصلي فله أن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r6.claim: What gives life is knowledge of religious teachings and laws: knowledge is life and ignorance is death.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r6.anchor: لما يحييكم } من علوم الديانات والشرائع ، لأن العلم حياة ، كما أن الجهل موت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r7.speaker: لبعضهم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r7.claim: An anonymous poem calls an ignorant person dead and his clothing a shroud, illustrating the claim that knowledge gives life.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r7.anchor: ولبعضهم : لا تعجبن الجهول حلته … فذاك ميت وثوبه كفن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r8.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r8.claim: Some explain the life-giving call as fighting unbelievers, since refusing it would let them overcome and kill Muslims, as in 2:179.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r8.anchor: وقيل لمجاهدة الكفار ، لأنهم لو رفضوها لغلبوهم وقتلوهم ، كقوله : { ولكم في القصاص حيواة }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r9.claim: Others understand it as martyrdom, citing the martyrs who are alive with their Lord in 3:169.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r9.anchor: وقيل للشهادة ، لقوله : { بل أحياء عند ربهم }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r10.claim: God may bring death before a person uses the present chance to make the heart sincere, treat its defects, and return it sound; therefore seize the opportunity for obedience.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r10.anchor: يعني أنه يميته فتفوته الفرصة التي هو واجدها وهي التمكن من إخلاص القلب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r11.claim: Another explanation says God can control a person’s heart and reverse intentions, turning fear to security and memory to forgetfulness; this does not remove responsibility for deeds of the heart.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r11.anchor: ويبدله بالخوف أمنا وبالأمن خوفا وبالذكر نسيانا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r12.speaker: المجبرة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r12.claim: The author rejects the Mujabbira claim that God blocks a disbeliever from faith and a believer from unbelief, calling this false doctrine.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r12.anchor: والمجبرة على أنه يحول بين المرء والإيمان إذا كفر ، وبينه وبين الكفر إذا آمن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r13.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r13.claim: A further explanation is that God knows whatever enters a person’s thoughts and that no inner secret is hidden from Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r13.anchor: وقيل معناه : أنه يطلع على كل ما يخطره المرء بباله ، لا يخفي عليه شيء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r14.claim: A reading doubles the rāʾ in ‘al-mar’; it drops the hamza and transfers its vowel to the rāʾ, then pauses in a form like ʿUmar.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r14.anchor: أنه قد حذف الهمزة وألقى حركتها على الراء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r15.claim: People are gathered to God, who rewards them according to the soundness of their hearts and sincerity in obedience.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p199#2/r15.anchor: فيثيبكم على حسب سلامة القلوب وإخلاص الطاعة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r1.claim: Istajībū means answer or respond; Kaʿb ibn Saʿd al-Ghanawī's verse uses the related sense of answering a call.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r1.anchor: قال كعب ابن سعد الغنوي . وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r2.claim: Responding to God means obeying His command; the response wording matches the summons that precedes it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r2.anchor: وإجابة الله تعالى هي طاعة أمره , وإنما خرجت عن هذا اللفظ لأنها في مقابلة الدعاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the summons is to faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r3.anchor: إذا دعاكم إلى الإيمان , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r4.claim: Mujahid says the summons is to the truth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r4.anchor: إذا دعاكم إلى الحق , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r5.claim: Qatada says the summons is to what is in the Qurʾan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r5.anchor: إذا دعاكم إلى ما في القرآن , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the summons is to battle and jihad against the enemy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r6.anchor: إذا دعاكم إلى الحرب وجهاد العدو , قاله ابن إسحاق

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r7.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r7.claim: ʿAli ibn ʿIsa takes it as what sustains their life in the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r7.anchor: إلى ما فيه دوام حياتكم في الآخرة , ذكره علي بن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r8.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ takes it as what revives their affairs in worldly life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r8.anchor: إلى ما فيه إحياء أمركم في الدنيا , قاله الفراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r9.claim: A seventh view takes the summons generally as encompassing everything God commands.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r9.anchor: والسابع : أنه على عموم الدعاء فيما أمرهم به

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r10.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet called Abu while he was praying; Abu hurried to answer, and the Prophet cited this verse when asking why he had not answered at once.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r10.anchor: روى العلاء بن عبد الرحمن عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة قال : مر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and al-Dahhak say God comes between a disbeliever and faith and between a believer and unbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r11.anchor: يحول بين الكافر والإيمان , وبين المؤمن والكفر , قاله ابن عباس , وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r12.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r12.claim: Mujahid says God may come between a person and their reason, leaving them unable to know what they are doing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r12.anchor: والثاني : يحول بين المرء وعقله فلا يدري ما يعمل , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r13.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r13.claim: Al-Suddi says a person cannot attain faith or unbelief except by God's permission.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r13.anchor: والثالث : يحول بين المرء وقلبه أن يقدر على إيمان أو كفر إلا بإذنه , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r14.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r14.claim: Qatada reads the phrase as God's nearness to the heart, preventing any secret or public matter from being hidden; it is a severe warning.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r15.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r15.claim: ʿAli ibn ʿIsa says death separates a person from the heart and prevents recovery of what was missed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r15.anchor: فلا يقدر على استدراك فائت . ذكره علي بن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r16.speaker: ابن الأنباري
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r16.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says God intervenes between a person and hopes held in the heart, such as survival, long life, victory, or conquest.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r16.anchor: وطول العمر والظفر والنصر , حكاه ابن الأنباري

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r17.claim: Another view says God controls what enters a heart as fear or security: believers become safe from their fear, while disbelievers fear His punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p307/r17.anchor: فيأمن المؤمن من خوفه , ويخاف الكافر عذابه

MUJAHID:v1p260#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p260#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p260#3/r1.claim: The call to what gives life is a call to the truth, meaning faith.
MUJAHID:v1p260#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله عز وجل ﴿ إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم ﴾ يقول إذا دعاكم للحق يعني الإيمان

MUJAHID:v1p260#3/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p260#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p260#3/r2.claim: God comes between the disbeliever and his heart, leaving him unable to understand.
MUJAHID:v1p260#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ يحول بين المرء ﴾ الكافر ﴿ وقلبه ﴾ حتى يتركه لا يعقل

MUQATIL:8:24-26/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r1.claim: Responding to God and the Messenger means obeying in the command to fight.
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r1.anchor: { يأيها الذين آمنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول } في الطاعة فى أمر القتال،

MUQATIL:8:24-26/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r2.claim: The promised fighting gives life by restoring the Muslims after humiliation and strengthening them after weakness.
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r2.anchor: { إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم } ، يعنى الحرب التى وعدكم الله، يقول: أحياكم بعد الذل، وقواكم بعد الضعف،

MUQATIL:8:24-26/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r3.claim: God turns the believer's heart between faith and disbelief and the disbeliever's heart between disbelief and faith.
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r3.anchor: { واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه } ، يقول: يحول بين قلب المؤمن وبين الكفر، وبين قلب الكافر وبين الإيمان،

MUQATIL:8:24-26/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r4.claim: People are gathered to God in the afterlife for recompense according to their deeds.
MUQATIL:8:24-26/r4.anchor: { وأنه إليه تحشرون } [آية: 24] في الآخرة، فيجزيكم بأعمالكم.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r1.claim: The pronoun is singular as in the preceding verse because responding to the Messenger is responding to God.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r1.anchor: وحد الضمير أيضا كما وحده فيما قبله لأن استجابة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وسلم كاستجابته

NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r2.claim: Responding means obedience and compliance; the call means summoning and urging.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r2.anchor: والمراد بالاستجابة الطاعة والامتثال وبالدعوة البعث والتحريض

NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r3.claim: What gives life is religious knowledge and law: knowledge is life, while ignorance is death.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r3.anchor: من علوم الديانات والشرائع لأن العلم حياة كما أن الجهل موت كما قال الشاعر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r4.speaker: الشاعر
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r4.claim: An unnamed poet likens an ignorant man in fine clothes to a dead man wearing a shroud, illustrating knowledge as life.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r4.anchor: لا تعجبن الجهول حلته فذاك ميت وثوبه كفن

NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r5.claim: Another explanation is fighting the unbelievers, since rejecting it would let them overpower and kill the Muslims.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r5.anchor: أو لمجاهدة الكافر لأنهم لو رفضوها لغلبوهم وقتلوهم أو للشهادة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r6.claim: The phrase may also mean martyrdom, as indicated by the statement that martyrs are alive with their Lord in 3:169.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r6.anchor: أو للشهادة لقوله تعالى بل أحياء عند ربهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r7.claim: God may cause a person to die before the opportunity to make the heart sincere passes; seize this chance and purify the heart for obedience.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r7.anchor: أى يميته فتفوته الفرصة التى هو واحدها وهى التمكن من إخلاص القلب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r8.claim: Alternatively, God intervenes between a person and the long life his heart desires, undoing his resolve.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r8.anchor: أو بينه وبين ما تمناه بقلبه من طول الحياة فيفسخ عزائمه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r9.claim: People will be gathered to God, who rewards them according to the soundness of their hearts and the sincerity of their obedience.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p61/r9.anchor: واعلموا أنكم إليه تحشرون فيثيبكم على حسب سلامة القلوب وإخلاص الطاعة

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r1.claim: The address is to believers who affirm the truth; Qurtubi says there is no disagreement.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r1.anchor: هذا الخطاب للمؤمنين المصدقين بلا خلاف

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r2.claim: Istijābah means answering; يحييكم loses a ḍamma for heaviness and cannot be assimilated.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r2.anchor: والاستجابة: الإجابة: و { يحييكم } أصله يحييكم، حذفت الضمة من الياء لثقلها.

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses استجيبوا as أجيبوا; normally the former takes لام and the latter does not, though استجاب can be direct.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: معنى «استجيبوا» أجيبوا ولكن عرف الكلام أن يتعدى استجاب بلام، ويتعدى أجاب دون لام

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r4.claim: لما يحييكم attaches to استجيبوا; the lām may also mean إلى.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r4.anchor: متعلق بقوله: «استجيبوا». المعنى: استجيبوا لما يحييكم إذا دعاكم. وقيل: اللام بمعنى إلى،

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r5.claim: A second gloss is that the call revives religion and teaches it.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r5.anchor: وقيل: اللام بمعنى إلى، أي إلى ما يحييكم، أي يحيي دينكم ويعلمكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r6.claim: Another gloss is reviving hearts through monotheism, metaphorically bringing them from unbelief and ignorance.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r6.anchor: وقيل: أي إلى ما يحيي به قلوبكم فتوحدوه، وهذا إحياء مستعار لأنه من موت الكفر والجهل

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r7.speaker: مجاهد والجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r7.claim: Mujahid and the majority take it as obedience to Quranic commands and prohibitions, bringing eternal life and blessing.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد والجمهور: المعنى استجيبوا للطاعة وما تضمنه القرآن من أوامر ونواهي

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r8.claim: Another view identifies the call with jihad, which brings apparent and eternal life; the latter is linked to 3:169.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r8.anchor: وقيل: المراد بقوله «لما يحييكم» الجهاد فإنه سبب الحياة في الظاهر

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r9.claim: Qurtubi prefers the majority's broad interpretation.

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r10.claim: Al-Bukhari relates that Abu Saʿid was praying when the Prophet called him, then cited this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r10.anchor:
روى البخاري
" عن أبي سعيد بن المعلى قال: كنت أصلي في المسجد فدعاني رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r11.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r11.claim: Al-Shafiʿi infers that doing a required act or utterance in prayer does not invalidate it.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r11.anchor: وقال الشافعي رحمه الله: هذا دليل على أن الفعل الفرض أو القول الفرض إذا أتى به في الصلاة لا تبطل

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r12.speaker: الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r12.claim: Qurtubi sees support for al-Awzaʿi: a praying person may call out and move to prevent a child falling in a well.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r12.anchor: قلت: وفيه حجة لقول الأوزاعي: لو أن رجلا يصلي فأبصر غلاما يريد أن يسقط في بئر

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r13.claim: Qurtubi says God creates human acquisitions of faith and unbelief, all good and evil.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24/r13.anchor: فبان بهذا النص أنه تعالى خالق لجميع اكتساب العباد خيرها وشرها.

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r1.claim: Qurtubi connects this to the Prophet's statement, By the Turner of hearts.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r1.anchor:
" لا، ومقلب القلوب "
وكان فعل الله تعالى ذلك عدلا

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r2.claim: God acts justly toward those led astray, withholding a grace they were not entitled to rather than a due right.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r2.anchor: وكان فعل الله تعالى ذلك عدلا فيمن أضله وخذله إذ لم يمنعهم حقا وجب عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r3.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says no one can believe or disbelieve except by God's permission and will.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r3.anchor: قال السدي: يحول بين المرء وقلبه فلا يستطيع أن يؤمن إلا بإذنه، ولا يكفر أيضا إلا بإذنه

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r4.claim: The heart is the seat of thought and belongs to God, who can block reason through illness; respond before losing the ability.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r4.anchor: والقلب موضع الفكر. وقد تقدم في «البقرة» بيانه. وهو بيد الله، متى شاء حال بين العبد وبينه بمرض أو آفة

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says God can intervene between a person and his reason so he does not know what to do.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: المعنى يحول بين المرء وعقله حتى لا يدري ما يصنع.

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r6.claim: In 50:37, having a heart means having intellect.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r6.anchor: إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r7.claim: Another view says death intervenes, leaving no chance to recover what was missed.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: يحول بينه وبينه بالموت، فلا يمكنه استدراك ما فات.

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r8.claim: At Badr, God could replace Muslim fear with security and enemy security with fear.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: خاف المسلمون يوم بدر كثرة العدو فأعلمهم الله أنه يحول بين المرء وقلبه

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r9.claim: A general explanation is that God changes things from one state to another.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: المعنى يقلب الأمور من حال إلى حال وهذا جامع

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r10.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r10.claim: Al-Tabari chooses the sense that God owns hearts more than people do and may intervene at will.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r10.anchor: واختيار الطبري أن يكون ذلك إخبارا من الله عز وجل بأنه أملك لقلوب العباد منهم

QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r11.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r11.claim: Al-Farra says the conjunction coordinates with the previous clause, or can begin a new sentence with وإنه.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:24#2/r11.anchor: وأنه إليه تحشرون } عطف. قال الفراء: ولو استأنفت فكسرت، «وأنه» كان صوابا

QASHANI:8:24-25/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:8:24-25/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:8:24-25/r1.claim: The believers addressed are those who believe in the unseen.

QASHANI:8:24-25/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:8:24-25/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:8:24-25/r2.claim: Respond by purification and refinement to what gives the heart life through true knowledge, or actualize faith and follow the path to God so He gives you life.
QASHANI:8:24-25/r2.anchor: بالتزكية والتصفية { إذا دعاكم لما } يحيي قلوبكم

QASHANI:8:24-25/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:8:24-25/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:8:24-25/r3.claim: If answering God and the Messenger is one response, the preceding account applies; if distinct, answer God inwardly through heart-works and the Messenger outwardly through works of the self.

QASHANI:8:24-25/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:8:24-25/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:8:24-25/r4.claim: Another distinction is to answer God through annihilation in unity and answer the Messenger by observing differentiated obligations and abiding through God.
QASHANI:8:24-25/r4.anchor: بالفناء في الجمع، وللرسول بمراعاة حقوق التفصيل

QASHANI:8:24-25/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:8:24-25/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:8:24-25/r5.claim: Act before readiness vanishes: God may come between a person and the heart by removing preparedness and producing a veil through sin’s rust.
QASHANI:8:24-25/r5.anchor: قبل زوال الاستعداد فإن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه بزوال الاستعداد وحصول الحجاب بارتكاب الرين

QASHANI:8:24-25/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:8:24-25/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:8:24-25/r6.claim: At the gathering to God, He repays each person from His attributes and essence according to their effacement and annihilation.
QASHANI:8:24-25/r6.anchor: فيجازيكم من صفاته وذاته على حسب محوكم وفنائكم

RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد والزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r1.claim: Abu Ubayd and al-Zajjaj gloss istajībū as ajībū, ‘answer/respond’; al-Razi cites a poetic usage as evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيد والزجاج { استجيبوا } معناه أجيبوا وأنشد قول الشاعر :

RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r2.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r2.claim: Most jurists hold that a command’s apparent force is obligation; al-Razi argues a merely recommendatory reading makes the command redundant, while the following threat confirms obligation.
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r2.anchor: المسألة الثانية : أكثر الفقهاء على أن ظاهر الأمر للوجوب ، وتمسكوا بهذه الآية على صحة قولهم

RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet called Ubayy ibn Kaʿb while he prayed; after Ubayy delayed, the Prophet reproached him with this verse, and Ubayy promised to answer future calls.
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r3.anchor: ما روى أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مر على باب أبي بن كعب فناداه وهو في الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi treats the Prophet’s rebuke of Ubayy as evidence that the verse requires answering; the command’s force is a probabilistic practical question, so a solitary report can support it.
RAZI-FULL:v15p117#2/r4.anchor: الاستدلال به أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دعاه فلم يجبه لامه على ترك الإجابة

RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r1.claim: The life-giving call cannot mean restoring already living people; since every divine command carries reward, the phrase applies generally to all commands.
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r1.anchor: وأيضا فلا يمكن حمل الحياة ههنا على نفس الحياة . لأن إحياء الحي محال . فوجب حمله على شيء آخر

RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r2.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r2.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the life-giving call with faith and Islam: faith revives the heart, whereas unbelief is its death; he adduces the verse about bringing the living from the dead.
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r2.anchor: قال السدي : هو الإيمان والإسلام وفيه الحياة لأن الإيمان حياة القلب والكفر موته

RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r3.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r3.claim: Qatada identifies the call with the Qur’an, which brings life, rescue, and protection because it causes knowledge, and knowledge is life.
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r3.anchor: قال قتادة : يعني القرآن أي أجيبوه إلى ما في القرآن ففيه الحياة والنجاة والعصمة

RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r4.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r4.claim: Most commentators identify it with jihad: weakening one enemy strengthens the Muslims; martyrdom grants lasting life; fighting can lead to the afterlife, the realm of enduring life.
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r4.anchor: قال الأكثرون : { لما يحييكم } هو الجهاد

RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r5.claim: A fourth interpretation takes the phrase as every truth and right, thus including Qur’an, faith, jihad, and all obedience; it means good, everlasting life promised to righteous workers.
RAZI-FULL:v15p118/r5.anchor: والقول الرابع : { لما يحييكم } أي لكل حق وصواب ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r1.claim: As related by al-Wahidi, Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak say God bars an unbeliever from obedience and a believer from sin; hearts are under God’s control, making people blessed or wretched as He wills.
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي حكاية عن ابن عباس والضحاك : يحول بين المرء الكافر وطاعته

RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r2.claim: Al-Razi argues that knowledge cannot be intentionally acquired without already knowing it is knowledge and its object, producing circular dependence; ignorance likewise requires prior ignorance.
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r2.anchor: أما العقائد : فهي إما العلم ، وإما الجهل .

RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r3.claim: Wills and motives cannot arise without a cause; if the human were their cause, each intention would require another intention, so God must create beliefs, wills, and motives.
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r3.anchor: وأما الدواعي والإرادات فحصولها إن لم يكن بفاعل يلزم الحدوث لا عن محدث

RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi concludes that both Qur’anic wording and rational proofs show that the states of hearts come from God, affirming the determinist account.
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r4.anchor: فنص القرآن دل على أن أحوال القلوب من الله ، والدلائل العقلية دلت على ذلك ، فثبت أن الحق ما ذكرناه

RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r5.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r5.claim: Al-Jubba’i argues that if God prevented someone from believing, that person would be incapable and the command absurd, like commanding someone to climb the sky or a disabled person to pray standing; he invokes the capacity rule.
RAZI-FULL:v15p118#2/r5.anchor: قال الجبائي : إن من حال الله بينه وبين الإيمان فهو عاجز ، وأمر العاجز سفه

RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r1.speaker: القائلون بالقدر
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r1.claim: The Qadarites argue that reading the verse as God blocking faith turns the command to obey into an excuse rather than the warning against disobedience that its context requires.
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r1.anchor: الوجه الثاني : أن الله تعالى أمر بالاستجابة لله وللرسول .

RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r2.speaker: القائلون بالقدر
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r2.claim: They argue that making the verse mean God prevents belief would let unbelievers use revelation as an argument against the Messenger: God prevented their faith while commanding it.
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r2.anchor: الوجه الثالث : أنه تعالى أنزل القرآن ليكون حجة للرسول على الكفار ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r3.speaker: القائلون بالقدر
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r3.claim: One interpretation is that God interposes death between a person and the use of the heart; obey and repent before death arrives. Al-Qadi says the following mention of gathering supports this reading.
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r3.anchor: الأول : أن الله تعالى يحول بين المرء وبين الانتفاع بقلبه بسبب الموت

RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r4.speaker: القائلون بالقدر
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that a person’s appointed term prevents the heart’s wishes from being fulfilled; the verse urges good works rather than reliance on hopes of a long life, using ‘heart’ for its contents.
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r4.anchor: الثاني : أن المراد أنه تعالى يحول بين المرء وبين ما يتمناه ويريده بقلبه ، فإن الأجل يحول دون الأمل

RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r5.speaker: القائلون بالقدر
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r5.claim: A further interpretation addresses Muslims’ fear at Badr: they should not refuse obedience because of weakness or cowardice, since God can replace those states with strength and courage as the turner of hearts.
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r5.anchor: الثالث : أن المؤمنين كانوا خائفين من القتال يوم بدر ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r6.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r6.claim: Mujahid takes ‘heart’ to mean intellect: act while rational, since loss of reason ends legal responsibility; heart can stand metonymically for intellect.
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد : المراد من القلب ههنا العقل فكان المعنى أنه يحول بين المرء وقلبه

RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r7.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r7.claim: Al-Hasan reads the phrase as God nearer to a servant than the servant’s heart, meaning nothing inward is hidden from Him; he compares God’s nearness to the jugular vein.
RAZI-FULL:v15p119/r7.anchor: قال الحسن معناه ، أن الله حائل بين المرء وقلبه ، والمعنى أن قربه تعالى من عبده أشد من قرب قلب العبد منه

QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r1.claim: God gives the people of tawhid life through the light of His unity after annihilating their awareness of all else and of temporal things.
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r1.anchor: وأما الموحدون فأحياهم بنور توحيده بعد ما أفناهم عن الإحساس بكل غير ، والملاحظة لكل حدثان

QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r2.claim: God guards and turns hearts as He wills, between guidance and misguidance, absence and union, veiling and nearness, certainty and doubt, intimacy and estrangement.
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r2.anchor: يصون القلب عن تقليب أربابها فيقلبها كما يشاء هو ، من بيان هداية وضلال ، وغيبة ووصال ، وحجبة وقربة

QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r3.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r3.claim: God keeps ordinary servants from laziness, aspirants from failure, and gnostics from deviation, enabling each group’s devotional progress.
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r3.anchor: ويقال صان قلوب العباد عن الجنوح إلى الكسل ، فجدوا في معاملاتهم ، وصان قلوب المريدين عن التعريج في أوطان الفشل

QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r4.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r4.claim: God blocks people from their own hearts so that their only return is to Him, without relying on other creatures or their own hearts.
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r4.anchor: ويقال حال بينهم وبين قلوبهم لئلا يكون لهم رجوع إلا إلى الله ، فإذا سنح لهم أمر فليس لهم إلا الأغيار سبيل

QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r5.claim: The person who turns to the heart at each new event differs from one who finds no direction except toward the Lord; a poem says the heart’s path to others is blocked.
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r5.anchor: وكم بين من يرجع عند سوانحه إلى قلبه وبين من لا يهتدي إلى شيء إلا إلى ربه ! كما قيل : لا يهتدي قلبي إلى غيركم

QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r6.claim: Scholars are those who have found their hearts, as in 50:37; gnostics are those who have lost their hearts.
QUSHAYRI:v1p388/r6.anchor: ويقال العلماء هم الذين وجدوا قلوبهم ، قال تعالى : { إن فى ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب }

STUDYQURAN:8:24/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r1.claim: What gives life may be the truth or the Quran, which gives life to the heart and brings commands leading to everlasting life in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r1.anchor: That which will give you life is the truth, or the Quran itself (Ṭ), meaning something that gives life to the heart

STUDYQURAN:8:24/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r2.claim: The call that gives life may also be the call to fight in God's way, since dying in that cause leads to everlasting felicity.
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r2.anchor: This verse could also mean that one should respond to the call to fighting in the way of God, since death in the way of God would lead to everlasting felicity

STUDYQURAN:8:24/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r3.claim: One interpretation is that God comes between a disbeliever and faith, or between a believer and disbelief.
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r3.anchor: interpreted to mean that He comes between a disbeliever and faith, or between a believer and disbelief (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:8:24/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r4.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that nothing, including the innermost dimensions of a person, is hidden from God, as in the image of His nearness to the jugular vein.
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r4.anchor: or that nothing is hidden from God, even the innermost dimensions of one’s being (Ṭ). In this sense it resembles the statement in 50:16

STUDYQURAN:8:24/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r5.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r5.claim: The phrase can mean God has power to change hearts, as when He changed the Badr participants' fear into security.
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r5.anchor: It can also mean that God has the power to change hearts, as when He changed the fear in the hearts of the participants of the Battle of Badr into a sense of security

STUDYQURAN:8:24/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r6.claim: The gathering of all creatures to God recurs throughout the Quran and connects with its repeated teaching that all things return to Him.
STUDYQURAN:8:24/r6.anchor: The notion of being gathered unto God is mentioned throughout the Quran (e.g., 2:203; 3:158; 5:96; 6:38; 23:79; 58:9; 67:24)

SULAMI:v1p264/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p264/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p264/r1.claim: Junayd reads the call as an inner journey: hear its sweetness, cut distractions, endure struggle, act faithfully, seize sound times, and live eternally through the Everlasting Real.
SULAMI:v1p264/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه في كتاب ' رواء التفريط ' في هذه الآية : قرع أسماع همومهم حلاوة الدعوة

SULAMI:v1p264/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p264/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p264/r2.claim: The soul's life is its purification from every defect in word and deed.
SULAMI:v1p264/r2.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه في قوله : ﴿ إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم ﴾ . قال : حياة [ النفس ] تصفيتها من كل معلول لفظا وفعلا

SULAMI:v1p264/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p264/r3.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p264/r3.claim: Respond to God in obedience so that your hearts may live.
SULAMI:v1p264/r3.anchor: وقال جعفر : أجيبوه إلى الطاعة لتحيا بها قلوبكم

SULAMI:v1p264/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p264/r4.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p264/r4.claim: Life through God is true life and gnosis, as expressed in the promise of a goodly life.
SULAMI:v1p264/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا : ﴿ إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم ﴾ قال : الحياة بالله هي الحياة وهي المعرفة ، كما قال الله :

SULAMI:v1p264/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p264/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p264/r5.claim: Answer God with your inner selves and the Messenger outwardly: the soul lives by following the Messenger, the heart by witnessing the unseen, and one gains modesty by seeing one's shortcoming before God.
SULAMI:v1p264/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : استجيبوا لله بسرائركم وللرسول بظواهركم ، إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم حياة النفوس

SULAMI:v1p264/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p264/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p264/r6.claim: Response has four levels: tawhid, realization, submission, and nearness.
SULAMI:v1p264/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : الاستجابة على أربعة أوجه : أولها : إجابة التوحيد

SULAMI:v1p265/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p265/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p265/r1.claim: God takes the hearts of His friends, veils them for their protection, and turns them through His attributes, sealing them with gnosis and stamping them with longing.
SULAMI:v1p265/r1.anchor: وأنه قيل : ﴿ إن الله ﴾ إشارة إلى قلوب أوليائه بأن الله يأخذها منهم ويحجبها لهم

SULAMI:v1p265/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p265/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SULAMI:v1p265/r2.claim: The Prophet said that the human heart lies between two fingers of the Merciful, who turns it as He wills.
SULAMI:v1p265/r2.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' قلب ابن آدم بين أصبعين من أصابع الرحمن يقلبها كيف يشاء '

SULAMI:v1p265/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p265/r3.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v1p265/r3.claim: Hearts undergo turning, while selves undergo transfer.
SULAMI:v1p265/r3.anchor: وسمعت النصرآباذي يقول : القلوب في التقليب والنفوس في التنقيل

SULAMI:v1p265/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p265/r4.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p265/r4.claim: The verse can mean that one's reason is turned over and one's understanding of God's address is turned away.
SULAMI:v1p265/r4.anchor: وقيل : ﴿ يحول بين المرء وقلبه ﴾ أي : عقله في التقليب وفهمه عن الله خطابه

SULAMI:v1p265/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p265/r5.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p265/r5.claim: God intervenes between a believer and faith and between an unbeliever and unbelief, returning each to what was decreed for them in eternity.
SULAMI:v1p265/r5.anchor: وقيل : يحول بين المؤمن والإيمان ، والكافر والكفر ، يردهما إلى ما سبق لهما منه في الأزل

TAB-FULL:v11p104/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says the life-giving call is to Islam, which brought people to life after the death of disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r1.anchor: عن السدي: " {يا أيها الذين آمنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم} [الأنفال: 24] قال: لما يحييكم فهو الإسلام، أحياهم بعد موتهم، بعد كفرهم

TAB-FULL:v11p104/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r2.claim: Mujahid says the life-giving call is to the truth.
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {لما يحييكم} [الأنفال: 24] قال: الحق

TAB-FULL:v11p104/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r3.claim: Qatada identifies it as the Quran, which gives life, chastity, and protection in this world and the next.
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {يا أيها الذين آمنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم} [الأنفال: 24] قال: هو هذا القرآن فيه الحياة والعفة والعصمة في الدنيا والآخرة

TAB-FULL:v11p104/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says it is the call to war, through which God honored the believers after humiliation, strengthened them after weakness, and protected them from their enemy after their oppression.
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r4.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: " {يا أيها الذين آمنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم} [الأنفال: 24] أي: للحرب الذي أعزكم الله بها بعد الذل

TAB-FULL:v11p104/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r5.claim: Tabari prefers obedience to God and the Messenger when the Messenger calls to life-giving truth; this includes jihad, Quranic judgment, good remembrance in this world, and eternal life in the Gardens hereafter.
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r5.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب، قول من قال: معناه: استجيبوا لله وللرسول بالطاعة إذا دعاكم الرسول لما يحييكم من الحق

TAB-FULL:v11p104/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r6.claim: Tabari rejects the Islam interpretation because the verse already addresses believers, so it would make no sense to order them to answer a call to Islam and faith.
TAB-FULL:v11p104/r6.anchor: وأما قول من قال: معناه الإسلام، فقول لا معنى له؛ لأن الله قد وصفهم بالإيمان

TAB-FULL:v11p107/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p107/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v11p107/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet called Ubayy while he was praying; Ubayy turned but did not answer, then explained that he was praying, and the Prophet cited this verse, after which Ubayy promised not to repeat that response.
TAB-FULL:v11p107/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على أبي وهو يصلي، فدعاه: أي أبي فالتفت إليه أبي، ولم يجبه

TAB-FULL:v11p107/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p107/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v11p107/r2.claim: In another report, the Prophet passed Ubayy while he was praying and called loudly; Ubayy did not answer, then promised to respond whenever the Prophet called, even during prayer, after the Prophet invoked this verse.
TAB-FULL:v11p107/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: مر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على أبي وهو قائم يصلي، فصرخ به، فلم يجبه

TAB-FULL:v11p107/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p107/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p107/r3.claim: Tabari says these reports do not make the verse specifically about answering a summons during prayer: it concerns the Messenger calling people, already Muslim, to life-giving truth, and Ubayy was Muslim at the time.
TAB-FULL:v11p107/r3.anchor: ما يبين عن أن المعني بالآية هم الذين يدعوهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى ما فيه حياتهم بإجابتهم إليه من الحق بعد إسلامهم

TAB-FULL:v11p108/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains that God intervenes between an unbeliever and faith, and between a believer and disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: " { يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: بين الكافر أن يؤمن، وبين المؤمن أن يكفر

TAB-FULL:v11p108/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God prevents the unbeliever from faith and obedience to God, and the believer from disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] يحول بين الكافر والإيمان وطاعة الله

TAB-FULL:v11p108/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas also describes God as intervening between a believer and disbelief and between an unbeliever and faith.
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: يحول بين المؤمن والكفر، وبين الكافر والإيمان

TAB-FULL:v11p108/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says God intervenes between an unbeliever and obedience, and between a believer and disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: يحول بين الكافر وطاعته، وبين المؤمن ومعصيته

TAB-FULL:v11p108/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak also says God intervenes between a person and becoming an unbeliever, and between an unbeliever and becoming a believer.
TAB-FULL:v11p108/r5.anchor: عن جويبر، عن الضحاك قال: «يحول بين المرء وبين أن يكفر، وبين الكافر وبين أن يؤمن»

TAB-FULL:v11p110/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says God intervenes between a believer and his disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم، في قوله: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: يحول بين المؤمن ومعصيته

TAB-FULL:v11p110/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God prevents the unbeliever from obedience and the believer from disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] يقول: يحول بين الكافر وبين طاعته، ويحول بين المؤمن وبين معصيته

TAB-FULL:v11p110/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r3.claim: Mujahid says God intervenes between a believer and disbelief and between an unbeliever and faith.
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: يحول بين المؤمن وبين الكفر، وبين الكافر وبين الإيمان

TAB-FULL:v11p110/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says God intervenes between an unbeliever and obedience, and between a believer and disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] يقول: يحول بين الكافر وبين طاعته، وبين المؤمن وبين معصيته

TAB-FULL:v11p110/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says God intervenes between believers and sins, and between unbelievers and faith.
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] يحول بين المؤمن والمعاصي، وبين الكافر والإيمان

TAB-FULL:v11p110/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r6.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r6.claim: Abu Salih says God intervenes between a person and sins.
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r6.anchor: عن أبي صالح: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: يحول بينه وبين المعاصي

TAB-FULL:v11p110/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r7.claim: Mujahid offers another explanation: God comes between a person and his reason, preventing him from knowing what he is doing.
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: يحول بين المرء وعقله

TAB-FULL:v11p110/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r8.claim: Mujahid also says God intervenes until the person is left unable to reason.
TAB-FULL:v11p110/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] حتى يتركه لا يعقل

TAB-FULL:v11p111/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r1.claim: Mujahid says Allah may interpose between a person and his heart until the person is left unable to reason.
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: هي يحول بين المرء وقلبه حتى يتركه لا يعقل

TAB-FULL:v11p111/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r2.claim: Mujahid asks how a person could act if God interposed between that person and his heart.
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: إذا حال بينك وبين قلبك كيف تعمل

TAB-FULL:v11p111/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r3.claim: Mujahid says God can block an unbeliever's heart from doing good.
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: يحول بين قلب الكافر، وأن يعمل خيرا

TAB-FULL:v11p111/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says a person cannot believe or disbelieve unless God permits it.
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r4.anchor: عن السدي: " {واعلموا أن الله، يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: يحول بين الإنسان وقلبه، فلا يستطيع أن يؤمن ولا يكفر إلا بإذنه

TAB-FULL:v11p111/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r5.claim: Qatada explains the phrase as God's nearness to the heart, comparing it with Q. 50:16.
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: " {يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] قال: هي كقوله {أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد} [ق: 16]

TAB-FULL:v11p111/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r6.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the general sense that God owns and controls hearts, withholding faith, disbelief, perception, or understanding from a person by His will.
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r6.anchor: أنه أملك لقلوب عباده منهم، وأنه يحول بينهم وبينها إذا شاء، حتى لا يقدر ذو قلب أن يدرك به شيئا من إيمان أو كفر

TAB-FULL:v11p111/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r7.claim: Al-Tabari argues that interposing between two things means placing a barrier between them; once God blocks a servant's heart, the servant cannot perceive what was withheld.
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r7.anchor: وذلك أن الحول بين الشيء والشيء إنما هو الحجز بينهما

TAB-FULL:v11p111/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r8.claim: Al-Tabari says the wording is general and includes all the reported senses; none is excluded unless binding evidence specifies one.
TAB-FULL:v11p111/r8.anchor: غير أنه ينبغي أن يقال: إن الله عم بقوله: {واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه} [الأنفال: 24] الخبر عن أنه يحول بين العبد وقلبه

TAB-FULL:v11p113/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p113/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p113/r1.claim: God controls believers' hearts and will gather them for recompense; Al-Tabari urges them to fear God and obey the Messenger so they do not incur punishment.
TAB-FULL:v11p113/r1.anchor: فاتقوه وراقبوه فيما أمركم ونهاكم هو ورسوله

TAB-FULL:v11p113/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p113/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p113/r2.claim: Al-Tabari urges believers to fear God, observe the commands of God and His Messenger, and answer the Messenger's life-giving call lest they incur divine anger and painful punishment.
TAB-FULL:v11p113/r2.anchor: فاتقوه وراقبوه فيما أمركم ونهاكم هو ورسوله أن تضيعوه، وأن لا تستجيبوا لرسوله إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم

TABATABAI:8:22-24/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r8.claim: The second command reinforces the earlier call to obey God and the Messenger and not turn away after hearing the truth.
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r8.anchor: إلى إطاعة الدعوة الحقة وعدم التولي عنها بعد استماعها

TABATABAI:8:22-24/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r9.claim: The Messenger calls to what gives human beings life by taking them out of ruin; God is nearer than their hearts and they will return to Him, so they should be heedful and resolute.
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r9.anchor: هذه الدعوة دعوة إلى ما يحيي الإنسان بإخراجه من مهبط الفناء والبوار

TABATABAI:8:22-24/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r10.claim: Life is the greatest blessing and highest possession of a living being, who sees only nonexistence beyond it; consciousness and will are sought-after effects of life.
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r10.anchor: الحياة أنعم نعمة وأعلى سلعة يعتقدها الموجود الحي لنفسه

TABATABAI:8:22-24/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r11.claim: Human beings are equipped to preserve spiritual life, the reality of their existence, just as created kinds are equipped to preserve themselves.
TABATABAI:8:22-24/r11.anchor: وقد جهز الإنسان وهو احد الموجودات الحية بما يحفظ به حياته الروحية

TABATABAI:8:15-29/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r1.claim: Human faculties identify benefits and warn of harms; innate divine guidance directs humanity toward its happiness, so its original constitution cannot err.
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r1.anchor: وهذا الجهاز الإنساني يشخص له خيراته ومنافعه، ويحذره من مواطن الشر والضر

TABATABAI:8:15-29/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r2.claim: People innately apprehend the happiness of their existence without doubt, as created kinds naturally move toward what benefits them; errors come from opposing influences that divert them toward harm.
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r2.anchor: كان من الحتم الضروري أن يدرك الإنسان سعادة وجوده إدراكا لا يقع فيه شك

TABATABAI:8:15-29/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r3.claim: He illustrates external misdirection with a heavy body that naturally settles on earth, rises only under an external force, and returns unless an obstacle diverts it.
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r3.anchor: كالجسم الثقيل الأرضي الذي يستقر بحسب الطبيعة الأرضية على بسيط الأرض

TABATABAI:8:15-29/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r4.claim: The Quran teaches that human nature recognizes right belief and action; the author cites primordial disposition, divine creation and guidance, responding to reminders, and purification of the soul.
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r4.anchor: فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم

TABATABAI:8:15-29/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r5.claim: People stray not because innate and divine guidance leads to ruin, but because they neglect reason, forget guidance, follow desire, and accept what Satan’s forces adorn.
TABATABAI:8:15-29/r5.anchor: بل لأنه اغفل عقله ونسي رشده واتبع هوى نفسه

TABATABAI:8:24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24/r1.claim: Following conjecture and desire conflicts with guidance already received from God; the author cites the person who makes desire a god.
TABATABAI:8:24/r1.anchor: إن يتبعون إلا الظن وما تهوى الأنفس ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى

TABATABAI:8:24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24/r2.claim: Truthful knowledge and action urged by human nature are requirements of happy life; they follow from that life and restore it when opposing influences weaken it.
TABATABAI:8:24/r2.anchor: فهذه الأمور التي تدعو إليها الفطرة الإنسانية من حق العلم والعمل لوازم الحياة السعيدة الإنسانية

TABATABAI:8:24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24/r3.claim: Turning from innate and divine guidance means losing beneficial knowledge and righteous action, becoming like the dead through ignorance and impaired will; only true knowledge and action revive a person.
TABATABAI:8:24/r3.anchor: فقد فقد لوازم الحياة السعيدة من العلم النافع والعمل الصالح

TABATABAI:8:24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24/r4.claim: The lām in limā yuḥyīkum means “to” (ilā), a common usage.
TABATABAI:8:24/r4.anchor: واللام في قوله { لما يحييكم } بمعنى إلى، وهو شائع في الاستعمال

TABATABAI:8:24/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24/r5.claim: The Messenger calls to the true religion, Islam, which the Quran explains as following human nature’s call to beneficial knowledge and righteous action.
TABATABAI:8:24/r5.anchor: والذي يدعو إليه الرسول صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم هو الدين الحق وهو الإسلام

TABATABAI:8:24/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24/r6.claim: Beyond ordinary worldly life until death, accompanied by awareness and voluntary action, the Quran describes a subtler reality of life.
TABATABAI:8:24/r6.anchor: وللحياة بحسب ما يراه القرآن الكريم معنى آخر أدق مما نراه

TABATABAI:8:24/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24/r7.claim: The world’s life is play and pastime while the Hereafter is true life; worldly preoccupation with illusions veils people from the more important aims of existence and spirit.
TABATABAI:8:24/r7.anchor: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان لو كانوا يعلمون

TABATABAI:8:24#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r1.claim: Human beings have a higher afterlife whose veil will be removed; it is free of play, idle talk, and sin, and is traversed by faith’s light and the spirit of servitude.
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r1.anchor: فللإنسان حياة أخرى أعلى كعبا وأغلى قيمة من هذه الحياة الدنيوية

TABATABAI:8:24#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r2.claim: He cites believers whose hearts hold faith and are strengthened by a spirit from God, and the person who was dead, then given life and light to walk among people.
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r2.anchor: أولئك كتب في قلوبهم الإيمان وأيدهم بروح منه

TABATABAI:8:24#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r3.claim: The Holy Spirit and revelation described as a spirit suggest a further life above the two already discussed.

TABATABAI:8:24#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r4.claim: A true life nobler and more complete than worldly religious life is attained through readiness formed by religion and entry into the company of the righteous.
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r4.anchor: يتلبس بها إذا تم استعداده بالتحلي بحلية الدين والدخول في زمرة الأولياء الصالحين

TABATABAI:8:24#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r5.claim: Accepting Islam’s true call brings real life, which also gives rise to Islam, beneficial knowledge, and righteous action.
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r5.anchor: فالتلبس بما تندب إليه الدعوة الحقة من الإسلام يجر إلى الإنسان هذه الحياة الحقيقية

TABATABAI:8:24#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r6.claim: He connects this life to God’s promise of a good life and reward for a believing man or woman who acts righteously.
TABATABAI:8:24#2/r6.anchor: من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فلنحيينه حياه طيبة

TABATABAI:8:24#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r1.claim: The wording is unrestricted: it can cover all the Prophet’s calls that revive hearts, any call embodying life, or their results in true happiness, including life near God in the Hereafter.
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r1.anchor: والآية أعني قوله فيها { إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم } مطلق لا يأبى الشمول لجميع دعوته

TABATABAI:8:24#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r2.claim: One interpretation, tied to the occasion of revelation, identifies the call as jihad, which revives the community’s cause and strengthens its religion.
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم إن المراد بقوله { إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم } بالنظر إلى مورد النزول

TABATABAI:8:24#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r3.claim: Another view takes the call as martyrdom in jihad, since God calls those killed in His way alive with their Lord.
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r3.anchor: وقيل المعنى إذا دعاكم إلى الشهادة في سبيل الله

TABATABAI:8:24#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r4.claim: The call is also explained as a call to faith, the heart’s life as unbelief is its death, or simply a call to truth.
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r4.anchor: وقيل المعنى إذا دعاكم إلى الإيمان، فإنه حياة القلب والكفر موته

TABATABAI:8:24#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r5.claim: One view identifies the call as the Quran and religious knowledge, since knowledge is life, ignorance death, and the Quran light, life, and knowledge.
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r5.anchor: وقيل المعنى إذا دعاكم إلى القرآن والعلم في الدين

TABATABAI:8:24#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r6.claim: Another view takes the call as a summons to Paradise because it contains everlasting life and eternal bliss.
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r6.anchor: وقيل المعنى إذا دعاكم إلى الجنة لما فيها من الحياة الدائمة

TABATABAI:8:24#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r7.claim: Each proposed interpretation can fit, but there is no reason to restrict the verse’s expansive meaning.
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r7.anchor: وهذه الوجوه المذكورة يقبل كل واحد منها انطباق الآية عليه

TABATABAI:8:24#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r8.claim: Ḥaylūla is interposition; qalb is the organ and often the Quranic locus of cognition and inward emotions, that is, the human soul acting through inner faculties.
TABATABAI:8:24#3/r8.anchor: الحيلولة هي التخلل وسطا، والقلب العضو المعروف

TABATABAI:8:24#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r1.claim: God creates and governs these faculties, giving or withholding them as He wills.
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r1.anchor: يتصرف فيها بإيجادها، ويتصرف فيها بتمليك الإنسان ما شاء منها كيف شاء

TABATABAI:8:24#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r2.claim: Other created things, like humans, have a self and attributes, powers, effects, and actions.
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r2.anchor: ونظير الإنسان في ذلك سائر الموجودات فما من شيء في الكون

TABATABAI:8:24#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r3.claim: God truly owns every created entity and all its attributes and appendages.
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r3.anchor: إلا والله سبحانه هو المالك بحقيقة معنى الكلمة لذاته ولتوابع ذاته

TABATABAI:8:24#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r4.claim: God makes created things owners of what He grants them; He remains the true owner between them and themselves and their attributes.
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r4.anchor: وهو المملك إياه كلا من ذاته وتوابع ذاته

TABATABAI:8:24#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r5.claim: God gives created beings what He wills and withholds what He wills.
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r5.anchor: وإعطائه ما أعطى، وحرمانه ما حرم

TABATABAI:8:24#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r6.claim: The same is true of all created things: God truly owns each entity, its attributes, powers, effects, and actions.
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r6.anchor: فما من شيء في الكون وله ذات وتوابع ذات من قوى وآثار وأفعال إلا والله سبحانه هو المالك

TABATABAI:8:24#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r7.claim: God is the intermediary between a person and their heart and is nearer than anything, as the Quran says He is nearer than the jugular vein.
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r7.anchor: وهو أقرب إليه من كل شيء كما قال تعالى ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد

TABATABAI:8:24#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r8.claim: As true owner, God is nearer to a person than their own self and faculties, which He grants and connects to them.
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r8.anchor: أقرب إليه حتى من نفسه وقوى نفسه التي يملكها

TABATABAI:8:24#4/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r9.claim: Resurrection reveals God’s sole true ownership and nullifies merely apparent ownership and authority.
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r9.anchor: فإن الحشر والبعث هو الذي ينجلي عنده أن الملك الحق لله وحده

TABATABAI:8:24#4/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r10.claim: The clause warns that God truly owns people and their hearts, is nearer than anything, and will gather them to Himself, when no other power can avail them.
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r10.anchor: فكأن الآية تقول واعلموا أن الله هو المالك بالحقيقة لكم ولقلوبكم

TABATABAI:8:24#4/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r11.claim: God interposes between each person and their heart and everything they own or are connected to.
TABATABAI:8:24#4/r11.anchor: فالله سبحانه هو الحائل المتوسط بين الإنسان وبين قلبه وكل ما يملكه الإنسان

TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r1.claim: When truth calls to monotheism, a person must answer: God is manifest truth, no veil can conceal Him, and no doubt or whisper can make one ignorant of His oneness.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r1.anchor: فإذا دعاه داعي الحق إلى كلمة الحق ودين التوحيد الذي يحييه لو استجاب له

TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r2.claim: God is nearer to the heart than the person is, so He knows its contents better than the person does.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r2.anchor: وإذا كان تعالى أقرب إلى قلب الإنسان منه فهو أعلم بما في قلبه منه

TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r3.claim: A person must answer truth inwardly as well as verbally, avoiding hypocrisy; God knows the heart and will disclose its contents at resurrection.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r3.anchor: فعلى الإنسان إذا دعاه داعي الحق إلى ما يحييه من الحق أن يستجيب دعاءه بقلبه كما يستجيبه بلسانه

TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r4.claim: Since God owns the heart, its faith, doubt, fear, hope, calm, and anxiety are related to His action through guidance, abandonment, or other divine nurturing.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r4.anchor: فما يجده الإنسان في قلبه من إيمان أو شك أو خوف أو رجاء

TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r5.claim: God acts in the heart as its true owner, according to His will, without being prevented or censured.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#2/r5.anchor: يتصرف بما شاء ويحكم بما أراد من غير أن يمنعه مانع

TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r1.claim: God’s unanswerable judgment and universal sovereignty support the claim that He alone governs the heart.

TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r2.claim: People must not regard faith, good intentions, or resolve as independently under their control: God truly owns the heart and can turn it from uprightness to deviation.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r2.anchor: فمن الجهل أن يثق الإنسان بما يجد في قلبه من الإيمان بالحق

TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r3.claim: Believers should commit to truth and good while fearing that God may turn them from happiness to misery, and should not feel secure from His plan.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r3.anchor: فمن الواجب عليه أن يؤمن بالحق ويعزم على الخير على مخافة من الله تعالى

TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r4.speaker: author
