TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r4.claim: Anyone whose heart resists truth and good should promptly answer God and His Messenger, not surrender to despair, because God can repair the inner state and turn the heart toward what is best.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#3/r4.anchor: عليه أن يبادر إلى استجابة الله ورسوله فيما يدعوه إلى ما يجيبه

TABATABAI:8:24#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r1.claim: The verse gathers profound divine knowledge: it removes disbelievers’ excuse for ignoring God, confronts hypocrites with God’s knowledge of their hearts, and teaches believers they do not independently own their hearts.
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r1.anchor: من أجمع الآيات القرآنية تشتمل على معرفة حقيقية

TABATABAI:8:24#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r2.claim: The teaching removes arrogance in those who imagine independent dominion and keeps them from being deceived by inner piety; it also relieves despair in those overwhelmed by desire and worldly diversions.
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r2.anchor: فيزول بذلك رذيلة الكبر عمن يرى لنفسه استقلالا وسلطنة

TABATABAI:8:24#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r3.claim: God’s interposition explains the command to answer God and the Messenger under every valid sense of the call to life.
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r3.anchor: على جميع التقادير من وجوه معناه

TABATABAI:8:24#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r4.claim: The verse’s meaning is broader than the interpretations reported by other exegetes.
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r4.anchor: أن الآية أوسع معنى مما أورده المفسرون من تفسيرها

TABATABAI:8:24#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r5.speaker: من قال
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r5.claim: One view says God is nearer to a person than their heart, as in the verse about nearness to the jugular vein, and takes this as a severe warning.
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r5.anchor: كقول من قال إن المراد أن الله سبحانه أقرب إلى المرء من قلبه

TABATABAI:8:24#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r6.speaker: من قال
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r6.claim: Another view says the heart cannot conceal anything from God, who is nearer to it than the person and knows it before its owner does.
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r6.anchor: وقول من قال إن المراد أن القلب لا يستطيع أن يكتم الله حديثا

TABATABAI:8:24#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r7.speaker: من قال
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r7.claim: A third view says God comes between a person and benefiting from the heart through death, urging prompt obedience before opportunity is lost.
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r7.anchor: وقول من قال إن المراد أنه يحول بين المرء وبين الانتفاع بقلبه بالموت

TABATABAI:8:24#5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r8.speaker: من قال
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r8.claim: Another view says God changes hearts between states, replacing fear of battle with security by intervening between people and their fearful thoughts.
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r8.anchor: وقول من قال معناه أن الله سبحانه يملك تقليب القلوب من حال إلى حال

TABATABAI:8:24#5/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r9.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r9.claim: A report from the Imams of the Prophet’s family says God prevents a person from mistaking truth for falsehood or falsehood for truth; no grading is stated here.
TABATABAI:8:24#5/r9.anchor: وقد ورد في الحديث عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أن المراد بذلك أن الله سبحانه يحول بين الإنسان

TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r6.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r6.claim: Al-Qummī reports that the ‘life’ to which God and the Messenger call is Paradise.

TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r7.speaker: أبو الربيع الشامي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r7.claim: Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Shāmī reports al-Ṣādiq saying the verse was revealed concerning the walāya of ʿAlī; versions through Ibn Mardawayh and Abū al-Jārūd attribute the application to al-Bāqir.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r7.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن أبي الربيع الشامي قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام

TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r8.claim: The reports applying the call to life to ʿAlī’s walāya are instances of application; the verse’s meaning is general.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r8.anchor: والرواية من قبيل الجري وكذا الرواية السابقة عليها، وقد قدمنا في الكلام على الآية أنها عامة

TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r9.speaker: أبو الجارود عن الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r9.claim: Abū al-Jārūd reports al-Bāqir explaining that God comes between a person and disobedience by directing him toward Hell, and between an unbeliever and obedience that would complete faith; deeds are judged by their endings.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#7/r9.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي عن أبي الجارود عن الباقر عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { واعلموا أن الله يحول

TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r1.speaker: هشام بن سالم عن الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r1.claim: Hishām ibn Sālim reports al-Ṣādiq interpreting the verse as God preventing a person from knowing falsehood as truth; al-Ṣadūq transmits the same report through Ibn Abī ʿUmayr.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r1.anchor: عن علي بن الحكم عن هشام بن سالم عن الصادق عليه السلام في قول الله تبارك وتعالى

TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r2.speaker: يونس بن عمار عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r2.claim: Yūnus ibn ʿAmmār reports al-Ṣādiq saying that a heart never becomes certain that truth is false or false is truth.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r2.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن يونس بن عمار عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال لا يستيقن القلب

TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet explained God’s interposition as preventing a believer from disbelief and an unbeliever from guidance; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī finds it close to al-Bāqir’s earlier explanation.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r3.anchor: عن أبن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن هذه الآية

TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r4.speaker: حمزة الطيار عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r4.claim: Ḥamza al-Ṭayyār reports al-Ṣādiq describing a person who desires an act through the senses but refrains because the heart rejects it as lacking truth; similar reports from al-Barqī and Jābir are traced back to the earlier explanations by Hishām and Yūnus.
TABATABAI:8:15-29#8/r4.anchor: عن حمزة الطيار عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام { واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه } قال هو أن يشتهي

TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r5.claim: Responding to God and the Messenger means obeying what they command and the matters to which they summon people.
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r5.anchor: أي أجيبوا الله والرسول فيما يأمرانكم به فإجابة الله والرسول طاعتهما فيما يدعوان إليه

TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r6.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r6.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī, agreeing with al-Farrāʾ, takes the call as jihad that revives the community's affairs and strengthens its religion with God's aid.
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r6.anchor: وقال الجبائي: أي دعاكم إلى إحياء أمركم وإعزاز دينكم بجهاد عدوكم مع نصر الله إياكم

TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r7.speaker: القتيبي
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r7.claim: Al-Qutaybī identifies the call with martyrdom: martyrs are alive with God.
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r7.anchor: قال القتيبي: هو الشهادة فإن الشهداء أحياء عند الله تعالى

TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r8.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says the call is to faith, which gives life to the heart, whereas unbelief is its death.
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r8.anchor: إلى الإيمان فإنه حياة القلب والكفر موته عن السدي

TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r9.claim: Mujāhid interprets the life-giving call as a call to the truth.

TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r10.claim: Qatāda says the call is to the Qurʾān and religious knowledge: ignorance is death, knowledge is life, and the Qurʾān brings learning, rescue, and protection.
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r10.anchor: إلى القرآن والعلم في الدين لأن الجهل موت والعلم حياة والقرآن سبب الحياة بالعلم وفيه النجاة

TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r11.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r11.claim: Abū Muslim takes the call as an invitation to Paradise, whose life and bliss endure forever.
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r11.anchor: ورابعها: أن معناه إذا دعاكم إلى الجنة لما فيها من الحياة الدائمة

TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r12.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r12.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says God may intervene between a person and benefiting from the heart by death, preventing recovery of lost opportunities; therefore obey promptly.
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r12.anchor: عن الجبائي قال وفيه حث على الطاعة قبل حلول المانع

TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r13.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r13.claim: Another explanation is that God is closer to a person than the person's heart, a severe warning; the continuation compares this with 50:16.
TABRISI:8:24-25#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه سبحانه أقرب إليه من قلبه وهو نظير قوله

TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda understand God to be nearer to a person than the person's heart, as in 50:16, a severe warning.
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r1.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة قالا وفيه تحذير شديد

TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r2.claim: Another explanation says God controls hearts, turning them between states; He could replace the believers' fear of battle with security.
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه سبحانه يملك تقليب القلوب من حال إلى حال كما جاء في الدعاء

TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r3.claim: Yūnus ibn ʿAmmār reports from Abū ʿAbd Allāh that a heart never becomes certain that truth is falsehood or falsehood is truth.
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r3.anchor: وروى يونس بن عمار عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: إنه يحول بين المرء وقلبه معناه لا يستيقن القلب

TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عن هشام بن سالم
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r4.claim: Hishām ibn Sālim transmits from Abū ʿAbd Allāh that God prevents a person from knowing falsehood as truth.
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r4.anchor: وروى هشام بن سالم عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says a heart cannot conceal anything from God, agreeing with al-Ḥasan.
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: معناه لا يستطيع القلب أن يكتم الله شيئا

TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r6.claim: People will be gathered to God for recompense on Resurrection Day: good for good and evil for evil.
TABRISI:8:24-25#3/r6.anchor: أي تجمعون للجزاء على أعمالكم يوم القيامة إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر

FARRA:v1p407/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p407/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p407/r1.claim: Respond to God and the Messenger when they call you to what revives your affairs.
FARRA:v1p407/r1.anchor: استجيبوا لله وللرسول إذا دعاكم إلى إحياء أمركم

FARRA:v1p407/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p407/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p407/r2.claim: God intervenes between a believer and disobedience, and between a disbeliever and obedience.
FARRA:v1p407/r2.anchor: يحول بين المؤمن وبين المعصية، وبين الكافر وبين الطاعة

FARRA:v1p407/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p407/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p407/r3.claim: وأنه is coordinated with واعلموا; beginning a new sentence with kasra would also be correct.
FARRA:v1p407/r3.anchor: و (أنه) مردود على (واعلموا) ولو استأنفت فكسرت لكان صوابا.

THALABI:v4p341#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p341#2/r8.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p341#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says the call is to faith, which gives life after the death of unbelief.
THALABI:v4p341#2/r8.anchor: فقال السدي: هو الإيمان يحييهم بعد موتهم أي كفرهم

THALABI:v4p341#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p341#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p341#2/r9.claim: Mujahid says it means the truth.

THALABI:v4p341#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p341#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v4p341#2/r10.claim: Qatada identifies it as the Quran, containing life, understanding, rescue, and protection in this world and the next.
THALABI:v4p341#2/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة هو هذا القرآن فيه الحياة والفقه والنجاة والعصمة في الدنيا والآخرة

THALABI:v4p341#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p341#2/r11.speaker: ابن إسحاق
THALABI:v4p341#2/r11.claim: Ibn Ishaq says it means war and jihad, by which God restored honor and strength and protected Muslims from their enemy.
THALABI:v4p341#2/r11.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: لما يحييكم يعني الحرب والجهاد التي أعزكم الله بها بعد الذل

THALABI:v4p341#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p341#2/r12.speaker: القتيبي
THALABI:v4p341#2/r12.claim: Al-Qutaybi explains it as what protects you, meaning martyrdom, and cites the martyrs as alive with their Lord.
THALABI:v4p341#2/r12.anchor: وقال [القتيبي] : لما يحييكم: لما يتقيكم، يعني الشهادة. وقرأ قوله بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون

THALABI:v4p341#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p341#2/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p341#2/r13.claim: Here the lām in لما means إلى, and responding means obeying; the report about Ubayy ibn Kaʿb illustrates the command.
THALABI:v4p341#2/r13.anchor: فاللام في قوله (لما) بمعنى إلى ومعنى الاستجابة في هذه الآية الطاعة يدل عليه ما روى العلاء بن عبد الرحمن

THALABI:v4p341#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p341#2/r14.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v4p341#2/r14.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet called Ubayy ibn Kaʿb while he was praying; after he hurried to answer, the Prophet cited this verse and asked why he had not responded sooner.
THALABI:v4p341#2/r14.anchor: العلاء بن عبد الرحمن عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة قال: مر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على أبي بن كعب

THALABI:v4p342/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r1.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v4p342/r1.claim: In the continuing report, Ubayy promises always to answer the Prophet, who offers to teach him a sura unmatched in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Quran: al-Fatiha, the seven oft-repeated verses.
THALABI:v4p342/r1.anchor: والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يمشي يريد أن يخرج من المسجد فلما بلغ الباب ليخرج

THALABI:v4p342/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v4p342/r2.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says God comes between an unbeliever and faith and between a believer and unbelief.
THALABI:v4p342/r2.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: معناه يحول بين الكافر أن يؤمن وبين المؤمن أن يكفر

THALABI:v4p342/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p342/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God separates an unbeliever from obedience and a believer from sin.
THALABI:v4p342/r3.anchor: ابن عباس: بين الكافر وبين طاعته ويحول بين المؤمن وبين معصيته

THALABI:v4p342/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r4.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p342/r4.claim: Mujahid says God intervenes so a person cannot reason or know what he is doing; another report from Mujahid says He blocks an unbelieving heart from doing good.
THALABI:v4p342/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يحول بين المرء وقلبه فلا يعقل ولا يدري ما يفعل، وروى خصيف عنه قال: يحول بين قلب الكافر وبين أن يعمل خيرا

THALABI:v4p342/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r5.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p342/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says a person cannot believe or disbelieve except by God's leave.
THALABI:v4p342/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: يحول بين الإنسان وقلبه فلا يستطيع أن يؤمن ولا أن يكفر إلا بإذنه

THALABI:v4p342/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r6.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v4p342/r6.claim: Qatada reads the verse as God's nearness to the heart: nothing a person reveals or conceals is hidden from Him, as in 50:16.
THALABI:v4p342/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: معنى ذلك أنه قريب من قلبه ولا يخفى عليه شيء أظهره أو أسره

THALABI:v4p342/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p342/r7.claim: When the believers were summoned to a difficult battle, God could replace their fear with security and cowardice with courage.
THALABI:v4p342/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو أن القوم لما دعوا إلى القتال في الحال الصعبة جاءت ظنونهم واختلجت صدورهم فقيل [فيهم] قاتلوا في سبيل الله

THALABI:v4p342/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p342/r8.claim: Another explanation is that God blocks a person from his intended goal, since death intervenes between hope and its fulfillment and prevents planning.
THALABI:v4p342/r8.anchor: وقيل: يحول بينه وبين مراده، لأن الأجل حال دون الأمل. والتقدير منع من التدبير

THALABI:v4p342/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r9.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v4p342/r9.claim: Al-Hasan reads the word with a doubled r and no hamza.
THALABI:v4p342/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: بين المرء، وبتشديد الراء من غير همزة

THALABI:v4p342/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r10.speaker: الزهري
THALABI:v4p342/r10.claim: Al-Zuhri reads it with a ḍamma on the mīm and a hamza; the source accepts both as valid Arabic forms.
THALABI:v4p342/r10.anchor: وقرأ الزهري: بضم الميم والهمزة وهي لغات صحيحة

THALABI:v4p342/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p342/r11.claim: People are gathered to God, who will recompense them for their deeds.

THALABI:v4p342/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p342/r12.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v4p342/r12.claim: Anas ibn Malik reports that the Prophet often prayed, O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm in Your religion; the Companions asked whether he feared for them.
THALABI:v4p342/r12.anchor: قال أنس بن مالك: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر أن يقول: يا مقلب القلوب ثبت قلبي على دينك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the command as answering God and the Messenger through obedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أجيبوا لله وللرسول بالطاعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r2.claim: Ataa reports from Ibn Abbas that they should hasten to what the Messenger calls them to from God's obedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r2.anchor: وقال عطاء عنه: سارعوا إلى ما دعاكم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إليه (¬3) من طاعتي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Zajjaj say استجيبوا means أجيبوا, supported by al-Ghanawi's line.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة والزجاج: معنى استجيبوا: أجيبوا (¬5)، وأنشد قول الغنوي: فلم يستجبه عند ذاك مجيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r4.claim: Al-Suddi identifies what gives life as faith and Islam: they give life to the heart while disbelief is its death; 6:95 compares living and dead.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r4.anchor: قال السدي: هو الإيمان والإسلام، وفيه الحياة (¬2)، وعلى هذا معنى الآية: أجيبوا الرسول إذا دعاكم إلى الإيمان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r5.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r5.claim: Qatada says it means the Quran, which brings life, salvation, and protection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: يعني: القرآن، أي: أجيبوه إلى ما في القرآن ففيه الحياة والنجاة والعصمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r6.claim: The Quran gives life through knowledge and beneficial practice, while ignorance is deathlike.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا القول: القرآن يحيي؛ لأنه سبب الحياة بالعلم، والجاهل حياته موت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r7.speaker: أكثر أهل المعاني وابن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r7.claim: Most authorities among أهل المعاني and Ibn Ishaq identify what gives life as jihad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r7.anchor: والأكثرون على أن معنى قوله: {لما يحييكم} هو الجهاد (¬6) وهو # قول ابن إسحاق (¬1)، واختيار أكثر أهل المعاني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r8.claim: Al-Farra says jihad revives their cause: warfare strengthens their power, while abandoning it weakens them and emboldens the enemy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r8.anchor: قال الفراء: إذا دعاكم إلى إحياء أمركم بجهاد عدوكم (¬3)، يريد أن أمرهم إنما يقوى بالحرب والجهاد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq says it means what leads to lasting life in the bliss of the Hereafter, with jihad as its means.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r9.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي لما يكون سببا للحياة الدائمة في نعيم الآخرة (¬5)، وسبب هذه الحياة: يعني الجهاد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r10.claim: Ibn Qutayba says it means martyrdom, because martyrs are alive and provided for; jihad leads to martyrdom.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r10.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: {لما يحييكم} يعني الشهادة؛ لأن الشهداء {أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r11.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r11.claim: Mujahid glosses it as the truth; the author says this can encompass the Quran, faith, and jihad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {لما # يحييكم} أي للحق (¬1)، وهذا يحتمل كل ما ذكرنا من القرآن والإيمان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r12.speaker: أبو علي الجرجاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r12.claim: Abu Ali al-Jurjani says it means Paradise, the enduring beneficial life, citing 29:64 and connecting this to Ataa's interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p86/r12.anchor: وحكى أبو علي الجرجاني في قوله: {لما يحييكم} يعني الجنة، واحتج بأن الحياة الدائمة النافعة حياة الجنة كقوله عز وجل: {وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak say God comes between an unbeliever and obedience and between a believer and disobedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس والضحاك: يحول بين الكافر وبين طاعته، ويحول بين المؤمن وبين معصيته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r2.claim: Ataa reports from Ibn Abbas that God prevents a believer from becoming an unbeliever and an unbeliever from becoming a believer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r2.anchor: وقال عطاء عنه: يحول بين المؤمن وبين أن يكفر به، ويحول بين الكافر وبين أن يؤمن به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r3.claim: Said ibn Jubayr gives an interpretation similar to Ataa's report.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r3.anchor: ونحو هذا قال سعيد بن جبير (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير في رواية خصيف
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r4.claim: In Khusayf's narration, Said ibn Jubayr says God blocks an unbeliever's heart from doing good.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r4.anchor: وقال (¬2) في رواية خصيف (¬3): يحول بين قلب الكافر وأن يعمل خيرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r5.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says no one can believe or disbelieve except by God's permission.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: يحول بين الإنسان وقلبه فلا يستطيع أن يؤمن ولا أن يكفر إلا بإذنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari identifies this as Mujahid's doctrine and al-Farra's choice: all affairs return to God, who determines the blessed and wretched; 21:23 is cited.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r6.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: وهذا مذهب مجاهد (¬5)، واختيار الفراء (¬6)، أي: فالأمور مردودة إليه، والسعيد من أسعده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r7.speaker: أصحابنا
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r7.claim: The author's school takes the verse as proof that hearts are in God's hand and He prevents faith or unbelief according to His will.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r7.anchor: قال أصحابنا (¬1): وهذه الآية دليل على أن القلوب بيد الله يقلبها كيف شاء، فإذا أراد الكافر أن يؤمن والله تعالى لا يريد إيمانه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r8.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r8.claim: Qatada says God is close to a person's heart and knows everything disclosed or concealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: معنى ذلك أنه قريب من قلبه، لا يخفى عليه شيء أظهره أو أسره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r9.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r9.claim: Abu Bakr explains this as God being nearer to a person than his heart, so nothing hidden escapes Him; 50:16 supports it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r9.anchor: قال أبو بكر: فيكون المعنى على هذا: أنه تعالى أقرب إلى المرء من قلبه، ولا تخفى عليه خافية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r10.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj describes this as God's nearness to a person, making the verse a stern warning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r10.anchor: وقال الزجاج: معناه: واعلموا أن الله مع المرء في القرب بهذه المنزلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r11.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj also reports that God intervenes between a person and what he puts off through death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r11.anchor: وحكى الزجاج قولا آخر وهو أن المعنى: أنه يحول بين الإنسان وما يسوف به نفسه بالموت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r12.claim: On the death interpretation, people should act rather than rely on hopes of survival and long life while postponing repentance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r12.anchor: أي: فاعملوا ولا تعتمدوا على ما يقع في قلوبكم من تأميل البقاء، وطول الأجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r13.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r13.claim: Mujahid is also reported to say that God comes between a person and his reason.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r13.anchor: وحكي عن مجاهد أنه قال: يحول بين المرء وعقله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r14.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r14.claim: Abu Bakr draws the lesson to act while rational and accountable, since one cannot be sure reason will not be lost.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p89/r14.anchor: قال أبو بكر (¬1): معناه: فبادروا إلى الأعمال وأنتم تعقلون فإنكم لا تأمنون زوال العقول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r1.claim: Here heart is a metonym for intellect, as in the verse about a reminder for one who has a heart.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r1.anchor: والقلب هاهنا كناية عن العقل كما قال في غير هذا: {إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r2.claim: Abu Bakr also relates an interpretation in which God intervenes at death; people should act while healthy and able to add good deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r2.anchor: وحكى هو (¬5): {واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه} بالموت فاعملوا قبل وقوعه، وأنتم أصحاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq offers a Badr interpretation: Muslims feared the enemy's numbers, and God could replace their fear with safety and the enemy's confidence with fear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r3.anchor: وذكر أبو إسحاق قولا آخر حاكيا وهو: أنهم كانوا يفكرون في كثرة عدوهم، وقلة عددهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r4.claim: Abu Bakr applies this to Badr: God could transfer the Muslims' panic to the polytheists and their bravery to the Muslims, bringing victory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p93/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر: وذلك أن المسلمين يوم بدر لما رأوا قلتهم في العدة, وكثرة المشركين جزع بعضهم فقال الله تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p94/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p94/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p94/r1.claim: Being gathered to God means being gathered for recompense for deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p94/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {وأنه إليه تحشرون} أي: للجزاء على الأعمال

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p178#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p178#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p178#4/r1.claim: God intervenes between a believer and sin, and between an unbeliever and obedience.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p178#4/r1.anchor: بين المؤمن والمعصية وبين الكافر والطاعة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p178#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p178#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p178#4/r2.claim: Another explanation is that God comes between a person and his desire.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r1.claim: Responding to God and the Messenger means obeying them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r1.anchor: { يا أيها الذين آمنوا استجيبوا لله وللرسول } أجيبوا لهما بالطاعة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r2.claim: What gives life means jihad: it strengthens their cause, brings martyrdom life with God, and leads to life in Paradise.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r2.anchor: { إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم } يعني: الجهاد؛ لأن به يحيا أمرهم ويقوى، ولأنه سبب الشهادة، والشهداء أحياء عند ربهم، ولأنه سبب للحياة الدائمة في الجنة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r3.claim: God intervenes between a person and their heart: one cannot believe or disbelieve except by His permission; He turns hearts as He wills.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r3.anchor: { واعلموا أن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه } يحول بين الإنسان وقلبه، فلا يستطيع أن يؤمن إلا بإذنه، ولا أن يكفر، فالقلوب بيد الله تعالى يقلبها كيف يشاء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r4.claim: People will be gathered to God for recompense for their deeds.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:24-25/r4.anchor: { وأنه إليه تحشرون } للجزاء على الأعمال.

ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r1.claim: The singular call is ascribed to the Messenger because the call is one: God's call appears through him, and his call is not distinct from God's.
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r1.anchor: Zira davet birdir. Allah’ın daveti Resûlünden zâhir olacak ve Resûlün daveti Allah’ın davetinden başka bir şey olmayacaktır.

ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r2.claim: The life-giving call is to knowledge or action that lifts people from an inanimate or animal state toward free, happy, eternal human life.
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r2.anchor: cemâdât ve behâim hâlinden çıkarıp insanlığın namzed olduğu muhtâr, mes‘ud, ebedî hayâta hürriyetinizle yükseltecek bir ilim veya amel

ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r3.claim: The Prophet was sent to summon people to this life, and hearing the call requires an immediate, eager response while they still have the opportunity.
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r3.anchor: Peygamber buna davet için ba‘s edilmiş ve insanlara kulak, dil ve akl ü irade bunun için verilmiştir.

ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r4.claim: God is nearer to and more sovereign over a person than the person's own heart; He knows its contents and controls them.
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r4.anchor: Ona kalbinden, kalbine ondan daha yakın, daha hâkimdir.

ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r5.claim: God can frustrate ambitions, change intentions, convictions, and tastes, turn a person against himself, remove reason and consciousness, and finally take life.
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r5.anchor: Azimlerini bozuverir, niyetlerini tahvil ediverir; kanaatlerini, zevklerini değiştiriverir.

ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r6.claim: Since people cannot resist when God separates them from their hearts or summons them to death, they must answer the life-giving call before that moment.
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r6.anchor: Allah sizinle kalbiniz arasına perde çektiği ve ölüme davet ettiği vakit icâbet etmemeye ve cebrine mukāvemet eylemeye imkân bulamazsınız

ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r7.claim: All people will be gathered to God alone and recompensed according to the rank of their deeds, so they should not excuse disobedience by appealing to the loss of heart or life.
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r7.anchor: Başkasına değil yalnız Allah’a toplanacaksınız da amellerinizin mertebesine göre cezâsını çekeceksiniz.

ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r19.claim: The warning itself shows how life-giving the Messenger's call is and reinforces the command to answer it.
ELMALILI:8:24-26#2/r19.anchor: İmdi bunları böyle bildirip de وَٱتَّقُوا۟ emrini tebliğ eden Resûl’ün ne kadar ihyâkâr bir davette bulunduğunu anlayın

MAJAZ:v1p245/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p245/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p245/r1.claim: Istajībū means answer or obey God; both istajabtu lahu and istajabtuhu are idiomatic, as Kaʿb ibn Saʿd’s poem shows.
MAJAZ:v1p245/r1.anchor: استجيبوا لله» (24) مجازه: أجيبوا الله ويقال استجبت له واستجبته، وقال كعب بن سعد الغنوى:

MAJAZ:v1p245/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p245/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p245/r2.claim: What gives life is what guides and reforms you and saves you from disbelief and punishment.
MAJAZ:v1p245/r2.anchor: إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم» (24) مجازه: للذى يهديكم ويصلحكم وينجيكم من الكفر والعذاب.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r1.speaker: Ebû Saîd el-Muallâ
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r1.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Mualla recounts that he finished praying after failing to answer the Prophet's call; the Prophet then cited this command and promised to teach him the Quran's greatest sura.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r1.anchor: Sahâbeden Ebû Saîd el-Muallâ anlatıyor: “Mescidde namaz kılıyordum. Resûlullah beni çağırdı, ona cevap vermedim, namazımı bitirince yanına gittim

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r2.speaker: İmam Şâfiî ve Evzâî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r2.claim: Shafi'i and al-Awza'i infer from the verse's wording and related hadiths that an obligatory or necessary act during prayer does not invalidate it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r2.anchor: İmam Şâfiî ve Evzâî gibi bazı müctehidler âyetin lafza bağlı yorumundan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r3.speaker: Evzâî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r3.claim: Al-Awza'i's example is that warning a child in danger while praying does not invalidate the prayer, since protecting life is obligatory.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r3.anchor: Evzâî’nin verdiği örnek şöyledir: Bir kimse namaz kılarken bir çukura veya kuyuya doğru ilerlemekte olan bir çocuk görüp

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r4.claim: Following the Prophet meant attending him and carrying out his orders; after him, it means following the Quran and Sunna and living accordingly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r4.anchor: Hz. Peygamber zamanında onun çağrısına uymak, yanında yer almak, emirlerini yerine getirmek nasıl çağrıya uymaksa

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r5.claim: The call benefits all humanity, not only believers, because the knowledge, faith, and practices God and the Messenger teach are life-giving.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r5.anchor: Bu çağrıya uymak yalnızca müminlerin değil, bütün insanların faydasınadır ve insanlığın meselesidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r6.claim: Taken broadly, life-giving includes biological health: religious commands contain rules for healthy living and fit human nature.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r6.anchor: Dinin emirleri sağlıklı yaşamanın kurallarını ihtiva ettiğinden, insan fıtratına uygun olduğundan, biyolojik mânada hayat vermektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r7.claim: Material confinement and deprivation of faith and spirituality contribute to stress, isolation, hopelessness, and fears that threaten mental and physical health.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r7.anchor: İnsanın ruh ve beden sağlığını tehdit eden stres, yalnızlaşma, ümitsizlik ve çeşitli korkuların önemli sebeplerinden birisi insanın madde dünyasında tutuklu kalıp

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r8.claim: Awareness of being with God and under His unmatched protection gives psychological strength and revives a person.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r8.anchor: Allah ile beraber olma ve O’nun eşi bulunmaz koruması altında bulunma şuurunun insana verdiği güç onu, psikolojik olarak canlı tutmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r9.claim: For those who see life as a test with duties and a hereafter, religion guides purposeful living and prevents life from being wasted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r9.anchor: Dünyayı bir imtihan yeri olarak gören, burada insanların bazı ödevlerinin bulunduğuna inanan

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r10.claim: Islam's root sense is peace and security; properly understood, its call seeks a world governed by law and justice without oppression, a call for global peace.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r10.anchor: İslâm kelimesinin kök mânası “barış ve esenlik”tir, doğru anlaşıldığında din olarak İslâm’ın da bir barış çağrısı olduğu anlaşılacaktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r11.claim: The idiom “between a person and their heart” refers to consciousness, reason, and feelings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r11.anchor: “İnsan ile kalbinin arası” ifadesi bir deyim olup bundan insanın şuuru, aklı ve duyguları kastedilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r12.claim: Nothing in a person's consciousness, reason, or feelings can be hidden from God; He knows and distinguishes sincere followers from those who only appear to follow for self-interest.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r12.anchor: Allah’ın çağrısına içtenlikle katılanlarla menfaati için öyle görünenleri Allah bilir ve ayırır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r13.claim: God can intervene in the inner realm beyond human access and change belief, knowledge, and feelings, so people should seek refuge in Him and ask Him to improve their inner state.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r13.anchor: Ayrıca hiçbir beşerin giremeyeceği, bilemeyeceği ve müdahale edemeyeceği bu alanlara Allah müdahale edebilir; inanç, bilgi ve duyguların değişmesini sağlayabilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r14.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r14.claim: The commentary cites the Prophet's prayer asking the Lord who turns conditions and hearts to make his state and heart beautiful.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:24/r14.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in duası için bk. Müsned, IV, 182; VI, 91

BAQILLANI:v1p55/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r1.claim: Incidental verse-like rhythm does not make speech poetry or its speaker a poet; poetry requires deliberate composition toward that form.
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r1.anchor: لم يصح أن يقال إنه شعر ولا إن صاحبه شاعر

BAQILLANI:v1p55/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r2.claim: A single accidental rajaz line is not poetry; some set a minimum of four rhyming lines, which the Qur'an never reaches, and its fragments also vary in rhyme.
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r2.anchor: وأما الرجز فإنه يعرض في كلام العوام كثيرا فإذا كان بيتا واحدا فليس ذلك بشعر

BAQILLANI:v1p55/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r3.claim: The Qur'an's challenge would have drawn imitation if it were poetry, since poets of one age can approach one another in that familiar craft.
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r3.anchor: ولو كان ذلك شعرا لكانت النفوس تتشوف إلى معارضته لأن طريق الشعر غير مستصعب على أهل الزمان الواحد

BAQILLANI:v1p55/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r4.claim: Arabic metrical speech needs equality in length and in its pattern of still and moving syllables; Qur'anic speech is not of that disfavored, uneven kind.
BAQILLANI:v1p55/r4.anchor: من سبيل الموزون من الكلام أن تتساوى أجزاؤه في الطول والقصر والسواكن والحركات فإن خرج عن ذلك لم يكن موزونا

BURHAN:v1p453/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p453/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p453/r1.claim: The reader who sees recitation as intimate address listens attentively, witnesses the meanings and attributes, sets aside habitual assumptions, and approaches the speaker with reverence and a sound, receptive heart; this station belongs especially to the people of the right.
BURHAN:v1p453/r1.anchor: الثالث من يرى أنه يناجى ربه سبحانه فمقام هذا السؤال والتمكن وحاله الطلب وهذا المقام لخصوص أصحاب اليمين

BURHAN:v1p453/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p453/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p453/r2.claim: Each word of divine address opens ten stations for the knower: faith, submission, repentance, patience, contentment, fear, hope, gratitude, love, and trust; these are the stations of the God-fearing.
BURHAN:v1p453/r2.anchor: أولهاالإيمان بها والتسليم لها والتوبة إليها والصبر عليها والرضا بها والخوف منها والرجا إليها

BURHAN:v1p453/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p453/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p453/r3.claim: The beloved's speech gives life to hearts: only a living person is warned by it, and only one who responds comes alive through it, linking the warning verse with the call to what gives life.
BURHAN:v1p453/r3.anchor: لأن كلام المحبوب حياة للقلوب لا ينذر به إلا حى ولا يحيا به إلا مستجيب

BURHAN:v1p453/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p453/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p453/r4.claim: Only people who traverse the ten stations witness the ten contemplative states; communion then makes intimate address unfatiguing and reveals divine attributes through the instruments of wording.
BURHAN:v1p453/r4.anchor: ولا يشهد هذه العشر مشاهدات إلا من يتنقل فى العشر المقامات المذكورة فى سورة الأحزاب

BURHAN:v1p453/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p453/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p453/r5.claim: The majesty of God's speech is veiled by the garment of letters: without that veil no created throne or creature could endure hearing it, and each person understands only the measure allotted by divine wisdom.
BURHAN:v1p453/r5.anchor: ولولا استتار كنه جمال كلامه بكسوة الحروف لما ثبت لسماع الكلام عرش ولا ترى

BURHAN:v1p453/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p453/r6.speaker: بعض العلماء
BURHAN:v1p453/r6.claim: A scholar maps Qur'anic sections onto landscapes: the mim openings are arenas, ra openings gardens, ha openings chambers, the glorification surahs brides, the hawamim brocades, and the mufassal surahs gardens; traversing them draws the seeker away from all else toward the vision.
BURHAN:v1p453/r6.anchor: قال بعض العلماء فى القرآن ميادين وبساتين وعرائس وديابيج ورياض فالميمات ميادين القرآن

BURHAN:v1p453/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p453/r7.speaker: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v1p453/r7.claim: The Prophet urges learning the Qur'an and seeking its rare matters, identified as its obligations and limits; he says it comprises lawful and forbidden rulings, clear passages, parables, and ambiguous passages, whose respective responses are to follow, avoid, act, believe, and reflect.
BURHAN:v1p453/r7.anchor: ولذلك قال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم اعرفوا القرآن والتمسوا غرائبه وغرائبه فروضه وحدوده

NAHHAS:v2p183/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p183/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p183/r4.claim: The nominative ending is omitted on the final yāʾ because it is heavy, and assimilation is not permitted.
NAHHAS:v2p183/r4.anchor: حذفت الضمة من الياء لثقلها ولا يجوز الإدغام

NAHHAS:v2p183/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p183/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p183/r5.claim: أن occupies the accusative position as the complement of واعلموا.

NAHHAS:v2p183/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p183/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p183/r6.claim: The clause beginning وأنه is coordinated with the preceding أن clause.
NAHHAS:v2p183/r6.anchor: وأنه إليه تحشرون ) عطف قال الفراء ولو استؤنف

NAHHAS:v2p183/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p183/r7.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v2p183/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says beginning a new sentence with إنّه, in the genitive-form opening, would also be correct.
NAHHAS:v2p183/r7.anchor: قال الفراء ولو استؤنف فكسرت وإنه لكان صوابا

ITQAN:v1p238/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p238/r1.speaker: حمزة
ITQAN:v1p238/r1.claim: At a stop, Hamza transfers the vowel of a final hamza after a silent consonant to that consonant, then deletes the hamza; examples include the phrase about a person and his heart and al-khabʾ.
ITQAN:v1p238/r1.anchor: فإنه يوقف عليه عند حمزة بنقل حركتها إليه فتحرك بهاء ثم تحذف هي سواء أكان الساكن صحيحا نحو

ITQAN:v1p238/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p238/r2.speaker: حمزة
ITQAN:v1p238/r2.claim: The same hamza-transfer rule covers final hamza after original yāʾ or wāw, whether long vowels or soft letters.
ITQAN:v1p238/r2.anchor: أم ياء أو واوا أصليتين سواء كانتا حرف مد نحو

ITQAN:v1p238/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p238/r3.speaker: حمزة
ITQAN:v1p238/r3.claim: When final hamza follows extra yāʾ or wāw, Hamza stops by assimilation after replacing the hamza with a like consonant.
ITQAN:v1p238/r3.anchor: وأما الإدغام ففيما آخره همز بعد ياء أو واو زائدتين فإنه يوقف عليه عند حمزة أيضا بالإدغام بعد إبدال الهمز

ITQAN:v1p238/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p238/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p238/r4.claim: There are 121 extra yāʾs not written in the consonantal text, 35 inside verses and the rest at verse endings; Nafiʿ, Abu Amr, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Abu Jaʿfar retain them in connected reading only; Ibn Kathir and Yaʿqub in both; Ibn Amir, Asim, and Khalaf delete them in both, with exceptions.
ITQAN:v1p238/r4.anchor: وياءات الزوائد وهي التي لم ترسم مائة وإحدى وعشرون منها خمس وثلاثون في حشو الآي والباقي في رؤوس الآي

ITQAN:v1p238/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p238/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p238/r5.claim: Some readers pronounce yāʾs omitted in connected reading when pausing, as in hād, āl, wāq, and bāq.
ITQAN:v1p238/r5.anchor: وأما الإثبات ففي الياءات المحذوفات وصلا عند من يثبتها وقفا نحو

ITQAN:v1p238/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p238/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p238/r6.claim: Some readers add final hāʾ of pause; the excerpt also lists feminine plural nūn, open nūn, and doubled forms as final additions.
ITQAN:v1p238/r6.anchor: وأما الإلحاق فما يلحق آخر الكلم من هاءات السكت عند من يلحقها في

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r1.claim: The phrase about being a thick-lipped black person implies a camel that cannot recognize the speaker’s kinship or follow his nobility.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r1.anchor: فلو كنت ضبيا عرفت قرابتي ولكن زنجيا غليظ المشافر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r2.claim: To say something has claws embedded in it represents attachment and domination by comparing it to a lion gripping prey or a hawk clutching its catch.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r2.anchor: في التعلق بالشيء والاستيلاء عليه حالة كحاله الأسد مع فريسته والبازي مع صيده

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r3.claim: Al-Ḥuṭayʾa may call himself the neglected guest and depict his own deprivation to mock al-Zibriqān and accuse him of abandoning guests to hardship.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r3.anchor: ( قروا جارك العيمان لما جفوته وقلص عن برد الشراب مشافره )

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r4.speaker: قالوا
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r4.claim: Some interpreters say Muzarrid meant foot but substituted hoof to satisfy the rhyme.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r4.anchor: فقد قالوا إنه أراد أن يقول بساق وقدم فلما لم تطاوعه القافية وضع الحافر موضع القدم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r5.claim: Despite the welcoming line that follows, Muzarrid’s hoof may retain a barb: it suggests the guest’s harsh journey and forceful effort driving the camel, in keeping with the earlier description of him as disheveled.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p27/r5.anchor: فليس بالبعيد أن يكون فيه شوب مما مضى وأن يكون الذي أفضى به إلى ذكر الحافر قصده أن يصفه بسوء الحال

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r1.claim: Even amid an age hostile to learning, the scholar should remain loyal to knowledge, a steadfast friend deserving more fidelity than other companions.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r1.anchor: فالعلم الذي هو صديق لا يحول عن العهد ، ولا يدغل في الود

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r2.claim: The rational disposition seeks to clarify what is obscure, untie what is knotted, reveal what is hidden, and strengthen the listener's confidence against doubt.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r2.anchor: والنزاع إلى بيان ما يشكل ، وحل ما ينعقد ، والكشف عما يخفى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r3.claim: Prior scholars' definitions of eloquence range from cryptic signs to pointers toward hidden treasure; their central insight is that discourse has arrangement, composition, and crafted form.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r3.anchor: فأجد بعض ذلك كالرمز والإيماء ، والإشارة في خفاء

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r4.claim: As crafted objects differ greatly in quality, discourse rises through ranks of merit until Qur'anic inimitability reaches a limit where aspirations and conjecture fail and all stand helpless.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p46/r4.anchor: حتى ينتهي إلى حيث تنقطع الأطماع ، وتحسر الظنون ، وتسقط القوى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r1.claim: The silk-weaving analogy wrongly treats composition as placing words and selecting positions; words form no composition unless the writer pursues grammatical meanings in their relations.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r1.anchor: لا يكون الضم فيها ضما ، ولا الموقع موقعا حتى يكون قد توخى فيها معاني النحو

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r2.claim: In Abu Tammam's line, the intended syntax makes his pen's ink the subject and snake venom the predicate, comparing its political writing to venom and its writing of gifts to sweet honey.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r2.anchor: وهذا المعنى إنما يكون إذا كان ' لعابه ' مبتدأ ولعاب الأفاعي خبرا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r3.claim: The same words can lose their intended image through a different grammatical reading; if word placement alone created the image, changing the parse without moving a word would not alter it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p279/r3.anchor: من غير أن يحول منه لفظا عن موضعه ، أو يبدله بغيره

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p97/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p97/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p97/r5.claim: What gives you life means jihad, which revives your religion and raises you in standing.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p97/r5.anchor: أي إلى الجهاد الذي يحيي دينكم ويعليكم.

DURR-FULL:v1p12/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Ubayy did not answer the Prophet's call while praying, after which the Prophet cited 8:24 and Ubayy promised not to do so again.
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وخرج على أبي بن كعب فقال: ياأبي - وهو يصلي - فالتفت أبي فلم يجبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r2.claim: Abu Saʿid ibn al-Muʿalla reports that the Prophet called him during prayer; after he finished, the Prophet asked why he had not answered and cited 8:24.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r2.anchor: ما رواه أبو سعيد بن المعلى قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r3.claim: The verse primarily means obey God and the Messenger, with “call” meaning guidance and “what gives you life” meaning what benefits you; the Prophet also applied the literal sense of answering a call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p94/r3.anchor: المعنى المسوقة فيه الآية هو الاستجابة بمعنى الامتثال
